entries.title: U.S. CISA adds Acronis Backup, Cisco ISE, and Google Pixel flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
entries.content:
## U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds Acronis Backup, Cisco ISE, and Google Pixel flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added [[1](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/09/16/cisa-adds-two-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog), [2](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/09/16/cisa-adds-one-known-exploited-vulnerability-catalog)] the following vulnerabilities to its [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog):

* [CVE-2026-76460](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-76460) (CVSS score of 10.0) Cisco Identity Services Engine Incorrect Use of Privileged APIs Vulnerability
* [CVE-2026-87886](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-87886) (CVSS score NA) Acronis Backup Incorrect Default Permissions Vulnerability
* [CVE-2026-58704](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-58704) (CVSS score of 8.8) Google Pixel Improper Authorization Vulnerability

[CVE-2026-76460](https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-ISE-ABP-VNSW7Tn5) is an authentication bypass vulnerability affecting an API in Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE). The flaw is caused by inadequate authentication checks on a specific API endpoint. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit it by sending a specially crafted request, potentially gaining unauthorized access to the affected system through its web-based management interface.

*“The Cisco PSIRT is aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability. Cisco strongly recommends that customers upgrade to a fixed software release to remediate this vulnerability.” [reads the advisory](https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-ISE-ABP-VNSW7Tn5).*

CVE-2026-87886 is a local privilege escalation vulnerability in Acronis Backup caused by insecure file permissions. The flaw affects the Acronis Backup plugin for cPanel & WHM and the Backup extension for Plesk. A local attacker with limited privileges could exploit the issue to manipulate files used by the backup service and potentially execute code with elevated, root-level privileges. Acronis reported exploitation in the wild in limited in limited, targeted attacks

Google has released its September 2026 Pixel security update, addressing a large set of vulnerabilities, including a high-severity flaw, tracked as [CVE-2026-58704](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-58704) (CVSS score of 8.0), in the cellular modem that has already been exploited in the wild.

The third vulnerability added to the KeV catalog is an Improper Authorization flaw tracked as [CVE-2026-58704](https://securityaffairs.com/199193/hacking/google-patches-pixel-modem-zero-day-exploited-in-targeted-attacks.html).

Google has addressed the flaw with the release of its September 2026 Pixel security update.

*“In Cellular Modem, there is a possible permission bypass due to a logic error in the code. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) escalation of privilege with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.” [reads the advisory](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-58704).*

The vulnerability is an elevation-of-privilege issue caused by a permission bypass resulting from a logic error in the modem code. Google said there are indications that the flaw may have been used in “limited, targeted exploitation.”

Unlike vulnerabilities affecting applications or higher-level Android components, CVE-2026-58704 resides in the cellular modem, a security-sensitive component responsible for communications between the device and mobile networks. The company warned that it has already been exploited in the wild.

*“There are indications that CVE-2026-58704 may be under limited, targeted exploitation.” [states Google](https://source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/pixel/2026/2026-09-01).*

As usual, the IT giant has not disclosed who exploited the vulnerability, how many devices were targeted, or what the attacks were designed to achieve.

The vulnerability is particularly notable because it does not require user interaction. According to the CVE record, exploitation can result in remote, proximal or adjacent privilege escalation without requiring additional execution privileges.

The technical details suggest that an attacker able to reach the vulnerable modem environment could exploit the permission bypass to obtain higher privileges. The attack vector is classified as adjacent rather than broadly Internet-facing, an important distinction when assessing the practical exploitation requirements.

In this case, however, Google has not publicly described the complete attack chain. There is also no evidence in the company’s advisory identifying the operation as the work of a commercial spyware vendor or a specific state-sponsored group.

According to [Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 22-01: Reducing the Significant Risk of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities](https://cyber.dhs.gov/bod/22-01/), FCEB agencies have to address the identified vulnerabilities by the due date to protect their networks against attacks exploiting the flaws in the catalog.

Experts also recommend that private organizations review the [Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) and address the vulnerabilities in their infrastructure.

CISA orders federal agencies to fix the GitLab and ConnectWise flaws by September 14, 2026, while the remaining JFrog Artifactory issues must be addressed by September 19, 2026.

**Follow me on Twitter:**[**@securityaffairs**](https://twitter.com/securityaffairs)**and**[**Facebook**](https://www.facebook.com/sec.affairs)**and**[**Mastodon**](https://infosec.exchange/@securityaffairs)

[**Pierluigi Paganini**](http://www.linkedin.com/pub/pierluigi-paganini/b/742/559)

**(**[**SecurityAffairs**](http://securityaffairs.co/wordpress/)**– hacking, [CISA](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/cisa))**

entries.title: Omarchy gains $18.5M in backing, fresh converts – and fierce critics
entries.content: In more than 30 years in the Linux business, we've never seen a distro win so much backing so fast – or make so many enemies. As we write, it's less than three weeks since we wrote about David Heinemeier Hansson's Omarchy Arch-based Linux. Much of Omarchy's success is due to the visibility of Hansson – better known as DHH – the man behind both the distro and the Ruby on Rails web framework. He has attracted considerable attention for posts critical of immigration, including As I remember London and Wolves, sheep, and gypsies. When we started work on that story, the organization established to fund and oversee Omarchy, the Omacom Foundation, claimed $8 million in backing. By the time we finished writing the story the next day, it was up to $10 million. But that was August, and Omarchy is gaining ground fast. In the short interval since then, Omarchy has had two more point releases and is now at version 4.0.3. The project has also announced Omarchy M, an initiative to bring the distro to Apple Silicon Macs, with support for older Intel models also planned. Even the website has been redesigned, with more internationalization – and an animation that follows the mouse pointer. (It's been quite a while since we've seen one of those.) The more important changes are less immediately visible. The Omacom Foundation says its pledges and donations have now reached approximately $18.5 million, a total that includes multiyear commitments and AI tokens. It has a list of Patrons, which now includes OpenRouter and Four Technologies, as well as DigitalOcean, plus token pledges from Meta Superintelligence Labs, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Fireworks. Indeed, the announcement says: "In fact, Omarchy Quattro has almost exclusively been built by agents. Because they're just incredibly good at stuff like bash, QML, and debugging Linux issues." Omarchy is already spending some of that money on people. Its first three announced hires are kernel developer Krzysztof Wilczyński, infrastructure head Emir Beganović, and the pseudonymous outfoxxed, creator of Quickshell, a core component of the Omarchy 4 interface. Omarchy very pointedly doesn't have a code of conduct; instead, it has a Doctrine, the first principle of which is "uniting the nerds." We have to say that that goal isn't going quite so swimmingly. Although it is winning supporters and boosters, lots of them, it is also attracting some hostility in the FOSS world. Brennan Kenneth Brown set out the accusation in a post titled Normalized Fascism in Open Source: $12 Million Given to DHH. Blogger Jürgen "tante" Geuter is blunt: "Omarchy should not matter. But sadly it does. As a power grab." He continues: "Running Omarchy means… willingly integrating oneself into a fascist community. Legitimizing it. Supporting it. Omarchy is a fascist project that normalizes fascist thinking for everyone entering that community (even unknowingly)." There's now also a Stop Omarchy campaign, with a banner: "Omarchy is a political movement disguised as a Linux distro." Most recently, prominent FOSS boffin Matthew Garrett weighed in, saying: "I cannot understand the mindset of a (I hope small) subset of the free software community that software-related freedoms can never be impinged upon, but it's fine to remove arbitrary other freedoms that have a greater impact on people's lives. "Omarchy is fundamentally incompatible with the goals of free software… It's bad because it is, at the technical level, bad – and it's also bad because it's idealistically bad." The Register asked the Omacom Foundation to comment. Code, cash, and culture wars The problem of open source developers not getting paid for their efforts is a persistent one in the FOSS world, and yet people and organizations are lining up to pledge money, or tokens, or both, to Omarchy. Its popularity is undeniable, but its creator's politics are likely a contributing factor. Hansson is not the only prominent figure in the software industry whose politics have attracted scrutiny. In July, we reported that the co-owner of Mullvad made a large donation to an anti-migration political party in Sweden. In Britain, the right-wing populist Reform UK party is also receiving large donations – which has since doubled. A year earlier, the XLibre project launched and explicitly rejected DEI. Some were angry, but others embraced it, including endorsement from Devuan. XLibre upset some folks so much that one of the developers behind Alpine Linux launched the Wayback server sooner than planned, in response to XLibre. At the time, we wondered if compromise and cooperation were possible, but that possibility seems remote now. From Brexit and the election and re-election of Donald Trump to Alternative für Deutschland winning a German regional election, right-wing populist movements have gained ground. Several observers have claimed that Omarchy isn't a distro as such: "Omarchy is not a Linux distribution in any traditional sense – in fact, the entire 'Omarchy distribution' amounts to little more than Arch Linux plus DHH's personal dotfiles." Even so, it is a brand – and one closely entwined with the politics of its creator. Other FOSS projects have embraced or endorsed right-wing values, but few Linux variants have placed them so prominently alongside the software. Omarchy is bold. It makes no effort to look familiar or be especially user-friendly, unlike beginner-friendly distros such as Linux Mint or Zorin OS. Its brand is that it's stylish and sophisticated; it uses Hyprland, a tiling Wayland compositor from a controversy-courting developer, with a keyboard-driven interface that makes no effort to work like any others. There are no window title bars, and Alt+F4 doesn't close a window here. It is designed to be different and new, embracing a steep learning curve. Its target market appears to be innovators, influencers, and AI-assisted developers. DHH is talking to users on X, and of course X's owner is no stranger to this area. It's working. Despite the criticism, Omarchy is attracting users, even previously Linux-averse ones, as well as donations. Populist movements attract supporters and win elections. Omarchy appears to be drawing some of that same audience to Linux. To paraphrase Winston Churchill, storm clouds are gathering over the free software scene, and we are underneath looking for any glimpse of a silver lining. For those who do not want to support these trends, we recommend Pop!\_OS 24.04 LTS and the COSMIC desktop. It is every bit as modern, bold, innovative, and striking. The distro underneath is a performance-tuned Ubuntu and, in our considered opinion, it works a great deal better. ®

entries.title: Ofcom discovers issuing Online Safety Act fines is easier than collecting them
entries.content: Ofcom chiefs have acknowledged that most fines issued under the Online Safety Act (OSA) remain unpaid, highlighting limitations in the comms regulator's enforcement powers. The regulator's director of enforcement, Suzanne Cater, told the House of Lords Communications and Digital Committee that although another payment arrived this week, "realistically the majority have not been paid." Ofcom has imposed fines totaling more than £7 million ($9.4 million) on 11 service providers under its OSA powers so far, but when asked, it refused to specify exactly how many have not paid, nor detail the payment that came in this week. Oliver Griffiths, group director at Ofcom, said the regulator's enforcement action had primarily focused on smaller companies in the pornography industry. Its largest fine under the OSA, for example, was the £1.4 million ($1.88 million) penalty imposed on 8579 LLC in February. However, Ofcom plans to pursue larger companies, which Griffiths said should make difficulties collecting fines less pronounced. "I think it looks acute at the moment," he told peers on Tuesday. "I think over time, as we are fining the bigger companies, if they're in breach of the act, this will be less of an issue." Asked why it had not collected more of the fines, Ofcom officials pointed to the limits of its powers and the ways online platforms structure their businesses to evade enforcement. Cater said the regulator was beginning to exercise its powers to hold senior managers personally liable in certain circumstances. She acknowledged, however, that its business disruption powers have limits. Ofcom cannot shut down a website globally, but it can ask a court to restrict access to one in the UK. It first invoked that power in May, applying for an order against an unnamed suicide forum whose operator it had already fined £950,000 ($1.2 million). Services do not escape the OSA merely by moving their operations and infrastructure overseas, as courts can order third parties such as ISPs to restrict UK access. However, business disruption measures require continuing noncompliance with the OSA and cannot be used solely to recover an unpaid fine. Griffiths said some services had complied after being fined but failed to pay the penalty, leaving Ofcom to pursue the debt separately – a potentially difficult process when a company has no UK assets. Ofcom regards disruption measures as a last resort. It would prefer to secure compliance before opening an investigation or, when collecting an unpaid penalty, register the fine as a judgment debt. The regulator told The Register that it was working with the UK government to consider strengthening these powers while preserving safeguards for fundamental rights such as freedom of expression. Cater insisted that Ofcom was showing its teeth despite criticism that the regulator had been too timid. "I think we are very active in using our enforcement powers," she told peers, pointing to the six active enforcement programs and 40 formal investigations covering more than 100 different services, including Telegram, TikTok, and X. An Ofcom spokesperson repeated Cater's figures, telling us: "We've been more active than any other regulator in the world when it comes to enforcing online safety laws." They added: "Some of the fines we've issued have been paid and some have not yet passed their deadlines to pay. Where deadlines have passed and we have yet to receive payment, we have initiated work regarding the pursuit of that debt. "If a company has assets in the UK, the process is relatively straightforward. If a company does not have assets in the UK, the process is more complex. Given this is an ongoing operational matter, we can't provide further details about specific companies." Plenty of enforcement, not enough impact Despite Ofcom's defense of its enforcement record, Griffiths said its own tracking metrics left him "underwhelmed" by the OSA's effect on online safety so far. He cited commitments from X to remove hateful and terrorist content more quickly, and from Meta and Snap to tackle grooming, as encouraging signs. "But I think [this is] a one-way ratchet that is going to be building up over time, and we're confident that the commitments that we've seen from some of the big services and the continuing momentum that we have is going to make a significant change over time," Griffiths said. The comments came a week after Children's Commissioner for England Dame Rachel de Souza told peers that children believed the OSA "has made absolutely no difference." Young people have little understanding of the legislation or how it aimed to change their online experience, de Souza said. She was especially critical of the legislation's focus on moderating content instead of looking to change online platforms' harmful and addictive designs. The hearing also turned to Meta's recent settlement of US claims that Facebook and Instagram harmed children. Lord James Knight asked whether the "eye-catching" agreement, worth up to $18 billion, would influence Ofcom's enforcement strategy. Griffiths said the case demonstrated both how much platforms might pay to settle online safety litigation and how effective enforcement could bring about changes to their services. ®

entries.content:
Models may not actually benefit from a native harness

![Melissa Pan](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/1873217404987133952/lk4l_593_normal.jpg)

Melissa Pan@melissapan

Does your Claude model really need Claude Code…? 🤔  
  
We evaluate 7 models on Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. Three surprising findings emerge:  
  
1️⃣Harness choice has little effect on task success rate, but can significantly affect the cost  
2️⃣A simple harness can be competitive  
3️⃣The native harness isn’t always the best.  
  
Millions of people are using coding agents, but the impact of harness choice remains unclear.

原文：[x.com/trevornoren/st…](https://x.com/trevornoren/status/2099201296717037791)

![Trevor Noren](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/1945104750162141184/MYdYB6hc_normal.jpg)

Trevor Noren@trevornoren

Alphaville: "The share of queries that are truly closed-weight frontier-model-worthy is declining. Back at the start of the year, 3/5s of its queries were routed through to closed-weight proprietary models. The latest share is just 1/4...OpenAI and Anthropic are private companies yet to list or issue rated debt. While totemically and technologically significant, companies at this stage of their lifecycle are really not supposed to be financially important...But their centrality to the industry that they dominate and the degree of circular financing in place means that this doesn’t look nailed on...The leading AI labs are cash-burning monsters, kept alive by the faith that their hyperscaler investors have in them. This is faith not only in the evident brilliance of their inventions, but also in the promise that their genius can be monetised at a pace that eclipses payments due to service debt, lease commitments, forward power agreements, the works."  
  
In my new report on "The AI Trade" ([sageroadresearch.com/products/the-a…](https://sageroadresearch.com/products/the-ai-trade)), I dive deep on the open-weight threat and what it could mean for investor expectations about the sustainability of Anthropic's and OpenAI's business models. To quote the report:  
  
"Since ChatGPT’s debut, AI has been a speculative bet on an unprecedented collective scale. There’s never been a clear path to profitability. There’s never been guarantees about the technology’s rate of improvement and timeline to game-changing enterprise transformation. From tech giants to financial institutions to retail investors, AI enthusiasm has rested on faith-driven patience—belief that the promise so many see in the technology’s current capabilities will at some point lead to future capabilities that generate skyrocketing profits. The question today: how much longer will that patience last?...  
  
It’s hard to overstate how much hinges on Anthropic's and OpenAI's IPOs. They will account for 13% of AWS revenue and 27% of Google Cloud revenue this year. As for Microsoft, OpenAI alone accounts for roughly 70% of its AI-specific revenue. OpenAI has committed to tens of billions of spending on chips. Deepening circularity concerns, tech giant earnings growth has been increasingly driven by paper gains in the private-market valuations of Anthropic and OpenAI. In Q2, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, Meta, and Microsoft reported $160b in cumulative “other income”, trouncing the $69b in “other income” reported in Q1. To quote the FT: “These one-off valuation boosts, derived in large part from enthusiasm around AI, risk distorting the financial picture at a time when investors are closely scrutinizing tech earnings.” If either Anthropic or OpenAI stumble, it’ll hit tech giants on multiple balance-sheet fronts. A pin-prick popping of the AI bubble may not be our base case, but if a pin is out there, it’s likely the revenue versus spending trajectories of Anthropic and OpenAI."

entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 17 日消息，近日有传闻称，问界品牌汽车将从明年 1 月 1 日起正式撤出鸿蒙智行和华为专卖店。经销商将自主选择华为、鸿蒙智行（其余四界）或问界品牌代理，问界将保留现有交付中心来支撑汽车售后与交付，如选择只做鸿蒙智行，经销商将保留直营模式。

[据IT之家此前报道](https://www.ithome.com/1/002/671.htm)，今年 9 月 15 日，鸿蒙智行发布了关于问界合作模式的说明，宣布即日起，问界将在鸿蒙智行合作框架下探索新合作模式：产品定义、产品设计、品牌营销、渠道零售、服务体系由赛力斯主导，华为终端参与赋能。所有问界用户的既有权益及后续服务不受影响。

entries.title: 数据中心建设持续面临民众阻力，硅谷最大城市圣何塞也不例外
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 17 日消息，据路透社今天（17 日）傍晚报道，硅谷最大城市圣何塞正面临一场围绕数据中心的争议。当地政府希望通过引入一批新项目，把圣何塞打造为 AI 基础设施中心，但居民和环保团体**纷纷组织起来反对这些计划**。

这场争议折射出美国各地政策制定者共同面对的难题：一方面，政商界普遍把 AI 产业视为维持经济竞争力的重要领域；另一方面，为 AI 提供算力的数据中心需要大量电力和水资源，还可能带来污染，公众对此越来越担忧。

这场争论在加州尤为敏感，因为谷歌、Meta、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等推动 AI 热潮的企业**都扎根于此**。

拥有近 100 万人口且身为加州第三大城市的圣何塞，选择积极拥抱数据中心扩张。当地估算，每座新数据中心每年可**贡献 300 万至 600 万美元**（IT之家注：现汇率约合 2,016.7 万至 4,033.4 万元人民币）**税收**，用于警务、消防、图书馆、道路和公园等公共服务。

硅谷虽然聚集了巨额财富，但不少居民**并不相信**，围绕 AI 数据中心展开的新一轮科技增长最终能够让整个社区普遍受益。

草根组织“我爱圣何塞大联盟”负责人之一埃琳娜 · 尹表示：“这些公司必须向我们证明，为什么它们有资格使用我们的资源，又准备怎样回馈社区。”

民众要求，当地在批准更多项目之前，应接受**更严格的公众审查**，更透明地披露能源和用水情况，并评估数据中心对居民健康和环境造成的影响。

圣何塞市长马特 · 马汉认为，答案不是停止建设数据中心，而是确保项目以负责任的方式推进。“人们完全有理由问：这会不会推高我的能源成本？会不会占用我们的清洁水资源？会不会降低这座城市的生活质量？这些问题**都非常合理**。”

**空气污染是另一项主要争议**。今年 4 月，由生物多样性中心牵头的联盟要求旧金山湾区空气质量管理局加强对数据中心柴油备用发电机的监管，理由是现行规定制定时，AI 数据中心尚未出现近年来这样的扩张规模。旧金山湾区空气质量管理局称，是否需要进一步加强保护措施仍在评估中。

提出其中多项法案的加州州参议员史蒂夫 · 帕迪利亚指出，许多全球最大科技企业都位于加州，因此加州**有责任率先处理**这些问题。

成员包括谷歌、Meta、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的数据中心联盟则表态**支持行业负责任地发展**，但另一方面，有关法案只把数据中心单独列为监管对象，却没有以同样方式对待其他大型工业和商业用电客户，并不公平。

entries.title: 德国法院裁定：Meta 需为 Instagram 和 Facebook 上的虚假广告承担责任
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 17 日消息，据路透社报道，德国一家法院当地时间周四裁定，Meta 应对第三方在其 Instagram 和 Facebook 平台发布的虚假广告承担责任，并要求这家美国科技巨头删除相关内容、支付赔偿金。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/8/373f8d53-b946-46bd-9bc3-694c7e7017dc.jpg?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

IT之家注意到，该诉讼由一家德国金融门户网站及其创始人提起。有人未经许可擅自使用了该网站的注册商标和创始人的照片，并推荐所谓的投资项目，而这些投资推广被指涉嫌具有欺诈意图。

法院表示，仅在 2024 年 8 月，该金融门户网站运营方就向 Meta 举报了近 260 起侵权事件。然而，部分相关内容在收到举报后最长经过 62 天才被删除。

法院同时认定，Meta 不能援引《数字服务法案》（DSA）中的“不知情”抗辩。法院认为，与单纯按照时间顺序展示内容的信息流不同，Meta 通过算法和广告机制对平台内容施加了控制，因此不能以事先不知道相关违法内容为由免除责任。

该法院还援引了欧洲法院今年 6 月作出的一项判决作为先例。

Meta 发言人在声明中表示：“我们对此判决持有不同意见，目前正在考虑下一步行动。”该发言人同时表示，公司已经采取了大量措施，包括主动检测相关内容以及删除用户举报的广告。

根据最新作出的判决，Meta 还必须披露这些虚假广告的具体信息，以及由此产生的相关收入。

法院表示，该判决目前尚未最终生效，Meta 可以通过提起上诉对判决提出异议。

entries.title: fix(ui): retain model choices while New Session refreshes (#150827)
entries.content:
``` fix(ui): retain model choices while New Session refreshes (#150827) ## What Problem This Solves Reopening New Session could show an empty model menu while refreshing, even when the same connection retained known choices. ## Why This Change Was Made NewSessionModelControl now reads the existing retained catalog for display while its replacement stays pending. This state has one writer. Fresh results keep the existing completion path. ## User Impact Known choices appear immediately. Accepted results update the open search; empty results clear it, and failures retain usable rows. Passive display cannot repair preferences or complete an account preview. Explicit model choices retain their runtime restrictions. ## Evidence The registered route fails before the fix and passes at desktop and mobile sizes. All 95 related owner tests and 33 browser tests pass on the combined source. The built Gateway's New Session and Chat flow passes. UI build, performance, formatting, lint and both line checks pass. ## Compatibility No persisted format, wire, SDK, plugin or migration change. Legacy browser and identified preferences are covered; no whole-package upgrade is claimed. ## Consumers Only New Session changes; Chat keeps its existing catalog owner. Production delta: +3 lines for display provenance and shared assignment. Growth accepted under the owner's standing acceptance (2026-09-15). ## Invalidation Existing connection, handshake, identity, agent, account and request-generation fences remain unchanged. No cache or timer is added. ## Tests Added retained remount, replacement/error/empty, no-write, runtime-selection and scope-fencing cases. Existing assertions remain intact. The regression fails on `0f20813457717561c029f90ee65ed2f622e023e5` and passes with this change: ```sh node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control.metadata-lifecycle.test.ts node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.model-catalog.e2e.test.ts ``` The combined-source proof also covers runtime choices, placement, preferences, catalog targets, catalog bootstrap, workspace memory and Chat picker refresh. The real-Gateway check uses runtime-matched UI assets after the performance comparison. ## Screenshots The replacement request is held in each before/after pair. All data is synthetic. | Before: reopened menu has no choices | After: retained choices appear immediately | | --- | --- | | | | | | |
Accepted replacement updates the open search
Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi ```

entries.title: 程序员不一定失业，而是主动离开公司！OpenAI总裁：一个人带着Agent，也能完成过去整支团队的工作
entries.content:
原创 姜篇 2026-09-17 17:29 北京

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=8e947502&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2FZhxqo7xEfgLibonjDdmqTatAU5d0micR4tSC0HzqicWJLa0pZku8HicQ9NgcheHtHXcKlYmjxDChggNrTGOAKSZORcnLsQF9aZRic9Fiae90oq0kw%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

程序员不一定失业，而是自己先离开公司！OpenAI总裁解释AI时代的新工作方式：一个人带着Agent，也能完成过去整支团队的工作

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=b6a4647d&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FMOwlO0INfQoIDJ0nx1IhNibpIpYLrpUE0kIP9qbF1iaY7EoZpaic6IojvbXibd5ZGiatxmjtibQRcVbGAPM9Ijvp66yQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=7c269b3a&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgK2HFedyg31dhKUYAZibUibl4MMywX6ia0x8RNYAeicibEZPFPxLnW861VRm7kpp97DKM9XTCqfkNSDGiaYxCqnkFFebUq65teh1WQMQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

编辑 | 姜篇

> 布罗克曼：“A wave of entrepreneurship.”
>
> 布罗克曼：一轮创业浪潮即将出现。

程序员不一定先失业，可能先离开公司。

OpenAI总裁布罗克曼说，他已经看到一些从业者辞职创业。AI让一个人能够完成过去需要一支团队才能推进的工作，开发者对公司的依赖正在下降。

> 布罗克曼：“Setting goals and being accountable for outcomes.”
>
> 布罗克曼：由人设定目标，并对最终结果负责。

Agent可以写代码、跑测试、检查漏洞，甚至操作软件完成长期任务。程序员的工作会逐渐从亲手执行，转向决定做什么、怎样验收，以及失败后由谁负责。

> 布罗克曼：“Young people can develop much faster.”
>
> 布罗克曼：年轻人可以成长得更快。

他的判断是，AI接走基础工作后，新人可以更早参与真实业务。

同一场访谈里，布罗克曼还谈到了几个已经发生的变化：Codex用15分钟找出13项网站安全问题；Astra可以连续工作24小时；1万个Agent被同时投入一个数学问题；OpenAI还暂停了部分生产工程师原来的项目，让他们转去建设安全系统。

这些变化指向同一件事：**AI对程序员的影响，不只体现在岗位数量上。公司会变小，团队会被重新分工，一部分开发者也会获得离开组织、独立完成产品的能力。**

**以下为访谈内容，我们进行了翻译与整理。**

## **四分之一生产工程师被临时调去“守系统”**

OpenAI最近经历过一次让内部高度紧张的安全事件。

布罗克曼在访谈中回忆，一款模型从受控环境中逃逸，随后进入了生产环境。团队没有把它当成一次普通Bug，而是立刻调整监控、沙箱和内部控制。

接着，OpenAI做了一个很重的组织决定。

> 布罗克曼：“原项目先停下来。你们现在负责防守，负责把安全架构提升一个等级，并用模型找出其中的漏洞。”

这里的“四分之一”，指OpenAI的生产工程师，不是全公司的四分之一，也不是宣布永久取消原有岗位。

但这个动作仍然说明了一件事：当模型获得浏览器、终端和生产工具后，安全不再只是上线前的一次审查。

模型能力每提高一截，工程团队都要重新检查权限、隔离和监控是否还挡得住它。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=c45db503&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgK4CqJ4xiaWx0OoRabyIb3u0OfyiacylBsInsHLmP2xKibaUT4iaN9609559E4yKa8vkF05CCTyVIibQLku5vviaCseZ0QTpsDpiazQQI%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*布罗克曼谈OpenAI暂停部分生产工程师的原项目，让他们转去升级安全架构*

*![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=235ddef7&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgIHlKfxrHIEkyUmhWBUfydicaqkLdraOBChdtc9EZVRNH10FP4EjZjbhvfkSkmFiasg1mrmXmUE927Jd3TrPkasAyKbRMSDaAVII%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)*

*Agent接走执行流程以后，工程师的时间会更多落在目标、验收、风险和责任上*

这比“AI会不会写代码”更接近开发团队眼下的问题。

代码生成更快以后，生产环境没有变简单。能够写出补丁的模型越多，团队越需要知道谁可以动哪些系统、修改完成后怎样验证、出错后由谁叫停。

## **Agent开始接管一整条工作流程**

布罗克曼举了一个自己的例子。

他让Codex检查个人网站。大约15分钟后，Agent返回了13项安全发现。接下来它没有停在“给建议”这一步，而是进入Cloudflare控制台，配置安全响应头，把网站迁移到Pages，并安排48小时后的复查。

> 布罗克曼：“15分钟后，Codex带回了13项安全发现。接下来的45分钟里，它直接操作控制面板，把修复做完。”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=afcff4fa&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJuS82EI48ibjGKkV8xia0rxicnJZFNmZ0nS9jJZFIA9bSSfRWNZu4GQ5ibzmKq6m67w463HKE1yUsnUfagSnzD8QMCD2xyjooxQ3w%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*Codex检查网站并返回13项安全发现*

变化发生在扫描之后。

过去的AI通常只会告诉开发者“这里可能缺少安全头”。新的Agent会继续登录后台、修改配置、迁移服务，再为自己安排后续任务。一次对话里的建议，开始变成一条可以自行推进的工作流。

布罗克曼把电脑操作能力看得很重。

他认为，Agent能走多远，最终取决于工具和上下文。屏幕、键盘、鼠标是人类使用软件的通用接口，模型一旦学会这套接口，很多没有API的旧系统也会进入它的工作范围。

> 布罗克曼：“对Agent任务来说，关键会落到工具和上下文。它需要看见环境，也需要知道前面发生过什么。”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=9e66343c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJNRtx2okVe8yFmfXklON5HNWicdrhTNJTVMIyxKrcw8gRCSE4ZxsmWmtedVgUMxciatD7ibK3r8VXjn0OiblotUAKjb29AaQPqbhY%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*布罗克曼谈工具与上下文对Agent能力的影响*

## **一个Agent不够，OpenAI开出一万名“数字研究员”**

单个Agent能接手完整任务，下一步就是让大量Agent同时工作。

OpenAI在Navier-Stokes实验里运行了1万个并发Agent。不同小组沿着不同研究路线搜索，彼此交换线索，Codex再把有价值的结果收拢起来。

> 布罗克曼：“我们在Navier-Stokes问题上使用了一万个Agent。”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=8a54e365&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgLBtuczakHMCnwvFN4Kb0s1iccOLBjCHS1HibGycP0lWAnByCicd8oEbTLZak5AP53qurXVfQWX7wAh19OibCHUx8WLlxjC35Vtegs%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*布罗克曼介绍OpenAI的一万个Agent并行实验*

OpenAI公布的数据很大：约270万条Agent消息、约1300亿输出Token。系统在启动约88小时后形成了一套解法，随后又花17小时用Lean做形式化验证。

这项结果仍然需要外部研究者继续复核，不宜写成数学界已经毫无争议地“彻底解决”。它更适合被看成一次多Agent工程实验：一个人很难同时维护上万条推理路线，系统却可以把它们分组、并行，再集中筛选。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=87483e9f&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgLwGWn8gLK8GobTTnUIibwuibdr8Jd4qoicyFz5lKCdJDDKVu4AwHkEUPzWmsQznB3HHpbcPbEo4OF8MXcjO74NzbYEvviaZtKlgsk%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*多Agent系统需要任务拆分、群组通信、结果汇总和独立验证*

对软件团队来说，这套结构并不遥远。

难点会从“谁来亲手改完所有文件”，转向“怎样拆任务，怎样防止重复劳动，怎样判断哪个结果可信”。

## **程序员的生产力单位从代码变成任务**

布罗克曼对长期Agent的描述，已经超出一次对话或一次代码生成。

> 布罗克曼：“Astra可以围绕长周期任务连贯工作24小时。能力还不均匀，但持续时间已经变了。”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=2fece36e&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgIGkU1NJlyTIRST3v5VhnGiaHxYpHIGlJtBwvPuzqLJzjdQmO8NLMq06ibJaaeQRibJIASBOoNJkCvz7NzPonaoicXibvIPV5xk8ZQY%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*布罗克曼介绍Astra连续工作24小时的能力*

如果Agent只能工作五分钟，开发者可以把它当成更快的补全工具。它能够持续工作一天，任务的边界就会扩大到“迁完一个服务”“查清一次故障”“完成一轮安全加固”。

程序员交付的单位也会跟着变化。

过去常见的计量方式是提交、代码行和完成的工单。多Agent环境里，更重要的数字可能是：一次任务调用了多少Agent，有多少结果被丢弃，人工在哪一步接管，最终是否通过验收，以及上线后有没有引发回滚。

少敲键盘，不会让工程师自动变成管理者。新的工作很具体：把需求写成可以执行的边界，给Agent准备上下文和工具，再对结果做最后判断。

## **公司会先变小，岗位不会原样保留**

布罗克曼预计，AI会带来一轮创业浪潮。

> 布罗克曼：“我们会看到一轮创业浪潮。很多人正在离开原来的岗位，因为这些工具让一个人能完成更多工作。”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=7f3ad271&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgIZylLAOicYSYveGOwoP8VgyoHlwY6w8YhlFycic3KmlhCnTxVNaY7MIWSzZ3kWib2IZ4vs7nwEoWibrLU0Gpk2tDP7935seu6IVaM%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*布罗克曼认为AI工具会推动更多人离职创业*

每个程序员都去独立创业并不现实，公司也不会就此消失。

更可能先发生的是，小团队能更早完成产品原型、基础设施和运营工具。过去需要前端、后端、测试和运维排队完成的第一版产品，可能由几个人加一组Agent跑出来。

分工还会存在，只是位置会变。当“做出第一版”越来越便宜，竞争会转向那些更难复制的部分：客户从哪里来，数据是否可靠，系统怎样进入真实业务，出了事故谁来承担损失。

对开发者来说，创业门槛降低是一面，岗位边界被压缩是另一面。

只承担明确执行任务的职位会先受到压力，能够把技术结果接到产品和业务的人更难被替换。

## **Agent接走基础任务后，新人靠什么成长**

访谈里有一个听上去很乐观的判断。

> 布罗克曼：“如果AI接走基础工作，年轻人可以更早参与真正的业务，也可能成长得更快。”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=6909ac0f&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJaOQfeCczGTDVAGloG3KrjcCyLYFHo2eujRia39vthsfwZUGAVA13uKHmf8GSOnCGIW3B22dAIiaSeDG4ZyaHaCpp2zhyS5icEME%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*布罗克曼谈AI接走基础工作后年轻人的成长路径*

问题在于，很多高级工程师正是从这些“基础工作”里长出来的。

如果Agent把这些环节全部做完，新人只看最后一张diff，很难知道模型试错了多少次，也不知道为什么某个看似更漂亮的方案不能上线。

团队需要主动重建学习路径。新人可以让Agent执行，但必须跟着一项任务走完问题确认、约束设置、执行记录、日志核对、上线和复盘。跳过手工劳动可以，不能把形成判断力的过程一起删掉。

## **安全团队只剩一个“防守窗口”**

布罗克曼认为，强模型刚出现、能力还没有大范围扩散的这段时间，是防守方少有的准备窗口。

攻击者最终也会获得相似能力。等到漏洞发现、利用代码生成和自动攻击都被模型加速，安全团队再靠手工响应就来不及了。

OpenAI想建设的“防御工厂”，会在新能力出现后自动扫描系统，发现漏洞、判断优先级、生成修复、部署并再次验证。

> 布罗克曼：“整条链路要跑起来：发现、分级、修复、部署、验证。下一款模型发布时，再把新的能力接进来。”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=68ca24d3&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgJibyLYcUgqk6GsYe1jnqCcQryQtkX5Cnye92q4yWagIp5GcDxHqs3dtHwcOeXx8oKwzyghsIG5PcibTIiaXkhTeFVBLxBVIDOFTc%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*布罗克曼描述持续运行的AI安全“防御工厂”*

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=931dd108&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgIySNZvqibtz7ibib90F0eseZgEr7Yib5pBg025EmHHFwECic5howm37NTY7HhCa26WicfOwrnNhZfS7YrAHSuCHFDkEpf42WPJMkUZI%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*AI可以加快安全修复链，但权限边界、人工确认和回滚路径仍需提前建设*

放进普通开发团队，这套做法可以从小处开始：让Agent持续检查依赖漏洞、权限变化和异常配置；每次修复必须带测试、执行记录和回滚方案；生产密钥、付款、删除数据和正式发布仍由人确认。

安全Agent要交付的结果，是把从发现到复测的时间压下来，而非再生成一份更长的报告。

## **目标和责任还在人的手里**

主持人追问，Agent越来越强以后，人还剩下什么？

布罗克曼的回答没有停在“人类有创造力”这种宽泛表述。他提到两件更具体的事：人负责设定目标，也要对结果负责。

> 布罗克曼：“设定目标、对最终结果负责，这两件事仍然很根本。人的价值也从来不只是完成一项项任务。”

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=4781926c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FZhxqo7xEfgLcLU3TLfZjarsKnmXx5sbW653QZZBjNjHhwTWO9icsSB1m7NpHQAnELXKcIkob9GKASM0rYU2H0pzvsRaFpCwhq3OG3A3NlT9A%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

*布罗克曼谈人类在目标设定和结果责任中的位置*

这句话放进软件工程里很好理解。

Agent可以修改支付系统的幂等逻辑，产品团队仍要决定历史订单怎样补偿；它可以给数据库迁移脚本补测试，工程师仍要判断灰度范围和回滚条件；它可以把所有测试跑绿，却不知道某个业务风险是否值得接受。

模型会完成越来越多动作，责任链不会自动跟着转移。谁决定让Agent接触生产数据，谁批准上线，谁在异常时叫停，这些安排必须写进系统和流程里。

## **“AGI时代”已经到了，能力仍然参差不齐**

布罗克曼在访谈中说，我们已经进入AGI时代。但他给“AGI”留了很大的解释空间。

> 布罗克曼：“AGI更像一段模糊的光谱，而不是某天突然跨过的一条线。”

他的依据来自任务持续时间和自主性：模型开始连续工作数小时甚至一天，可以记住上下文、使用工具并主动推进。但能力仍然“参差不齐”，某些任务很强，换个环境又会犯低级错误。

开发团队可以暂时放下“AGI到底算不算到来”这场争论。

更实用的判断是：在你自己的仓库里，Agent能够独立工作多久；它在哪些步骤会失去上下文；失败能否被测试、日志和权限系统及时拦住。

## **评论区：效率提高一百倍，还是一场AGI营销**

一位从历史学转向3D建模和游戏开发的网友说，自己刚装Codex一周，部分流程已经快了100倍，还能做过去做不了的东西。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=e57214f0&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgIvGcWLpevUevBxcQwpwic4H7wujWickZLMgeVowPhjMAsopz3PLWYJNhhH4NVlKJjnMqSGf2IrFQF5511iaSHYruvBnP65ia3LfFU%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*YouTube网友分享使用Codex后的效率变化*

另一位网友抓住了新人培养的矛盾：新人过去靠基础工作学习，AI接走基础工作以后，他们究竟从哪里获得经验？

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=b7d1ea8f&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgKZoAib11XREKEDoOw8e4gAic1rTrHS1lucDaNicPUFgfm8DKPG3WvXR1Ddef9XaCKAzschFx8n7QnL4JtgBhug6xyzMjdkibN3gibU%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*YouTube网友讽刺“跳过基础工作就能更快成长”的说法*

布罗克曼宣布“AGI时代已经到来”，也引来了对利益关系的质疑。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=68d7df42&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgLRicMBLP2R6qsdj3HHibiatzQJqAMywV6DJQzCm9FlcWBrd1GVRjfib4OuVKsMDUgcG4Nkwxz1lybxS3eMDiaEHc7ezxV73KmtkLac%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*YouTube网友质疑AGI叙事与OpenAI自身利益的关系*

还有人担心，安全会不会变成限制普通人使用能力的理由，而少数机构继续掌握最强模型。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=e2c7964f&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FZhxqo7xEfgItPVOjpibgSUwU8fj7icv7D7oA1EwH0IORDVfzk8qtU3rkfWUQZfKVd2PSToQNSXdhUDWOxMR523z2VZMZBbhjnd0ibhKwiaINDwU%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

*YouTube网友质疑前沿模型能力和安全权力是否会集中在少数机构*

## **写在最后**

“AGI时代来了”很适合做传播，OpenAI内部已经发生的组织变化更值得看。

更具体的信号已经出现在OpenAI内部：四分之一生产工程师可以被临时调去建设安全系统，一个Agent能够在网站后台连续执行一整条任务，一万个Agent可以围绕同一问题并行搜索。

程序员不会在某个早晨集体消失，岗位也很难原样保留。重复执行会继续交给Agent，任务拆分、上下文准备、结果验证、安全控制和事故责任会占据更多时间。

下一阶段的工程师，不能只证明自己比模型写得快。他要让一组能力不稳定、权限各不相同的Agent，在真实系统里完成工作，同时知道什么时候该停下来。

AI越强，人类创造力反而越值钱！诺奖得主哈萨比斯：未来十年可能迎来一场“新文艺复兴”

entries.title: 'Zuckoff' App Detects Meta Smartglasses, as Meta Plans Camera-Free Version, Loses Money, and Offers Social Media Subscriptions
entries.content:
The New York Post reports:
A new app called Zuckoff can detect if a user is near someone with Meta's creepy AI-powered glasses, which have drawn criticism for enabling creeps to record video of women without their consent. Programmer Pawel Szydlowski says tales of dirtbags recording themselves perving on women or harassing strangers prompted him to launch the app...
Zuckoff — which detects Bluetooth signatures broadcast by smart glasses and can estimate their distance — has gained some 5,000 users since it hit Apple's App Store last month, according to Business Insider. "There's a need for such an application," the 30-year-old Polish techie told the outlet, adding that European Union regulators have contacted him for more info about his app. "We as a society have the right to at least know that someone is recording," Szydlowski said...
Earlier this month, the tech giant disabled thousands of glasses it found had been tampered with to keep a small light off that indicates the device is recording.
It's already #77 on the iPhone's list of best-selling utilities apps.
In a related story, "After accusations of selling 'perv glasses,' Meta prepares to sell a pair without a camera," writes TechCrunch, citing a report from The Information.
The glasses include six built-in microphones so users can communicate with the chatbot, as well as a button on the side of the glasses that, when pressed, activates the AI system... Meta's Reality Labs, which is responsible for developing its smart glasses line, is still losing a gargantuan amount of money, as its earnings report from April revealed.
In fact, Meta stock is off 13% over the last 12 months, reports Yahoo Finance. So Tuesday Meta announced subscription services for its social apps as "part of Meta's push to drive additional revenue from the billions it's investing in AI data centers and model development."
The plans, which start at $2.99 per month for single-product plans, $7.99 for individual bundles, and $14.99 for creator and business bundles, provide a number of features for users looking to get more out of their Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp accounts. Instagram Plus and Facebook Plus allow users to keep their stories up for 48 hours instead of 24, send animated super reactions and super hearts to stories, preview stories without showing up as a viewer in other users' lists, and more. WhatsApp Plus lets you share exclusive stickers, get exclusive ringtones for contacts, and pin up to 20 different chats.
Meta One also includes Core and Premium user plans that offer the features found in the single-product plans, along with increased AI usage limits for images and videos. The social media giant is also offering creator and business plans... that it says include capabilities such as enhanced profiles, automatic follow invitations to users that interact with your content, and increased access to the Meta Business Agent, which can respond on your behalf.
When Instagram head Adam Mosseri announced on Threads that the plans brought "more features and more AI across Instagram, WhatsApp, Facebook, and Meta AI," writer Joe Hill drew 13,300 likes for his response. "That's sweet--so pay a fee, get more AI, pay nothing, get a little less AI. Can we work out a deal where you pay ME and I get no AI at all?"

entries.title: Test environment let anyone access live customer data
entries.content: PWNED Welcome back to PWNED, the weekly column where we learn important life lessons about how we let cybercrims access our data through carelessness. Hopefully, others’ mistakes provide an example of what not to do. Today’s tales of woe comes courtesy of Richard Schut, Managing Director & AI Software Researcher at SmartRepl, a company that offers business AI services such as AI receptionists and sales automation. In a past job, Schut was working for what he describes as a mid-size company during a security audit whose purpose was to identify any potential problems ahead of moving some local systems to the cloud. Schut and his team discovered that there was a test environment that was accessible outside the network and connected to a database which had live customer information in it. This was a gaping hole that a miscreant could have used to grab valuable information from the business. “What made the situation particularly concerning was that the environment had originally been created for what the development team considered a short-term purpose,” he told The Register. “They needed somewhere to demonstrate the application and test the migration, so a staging instance was spun up quickly. It was never intended to become part of the company's permanent infrastructure.” Unfortunately, the test environment was still running months after it was initially set up. And because those who created it did not expect unauthorized people to access it, they didn’t use the same authentication and access control methods that they would in production. The SQL file containing the database was appropriately named master\_test\_final.sql, just in case there was any question about what it contained. “It was a classic example of how security problems don't always come from sophisticated attacks or exotic vulnerabilities,” Schut said. “Sometimes the biggest risk is simply something that was supposed to exist for a few hours, but was still sitting there six months later.” After Schut and his colleagues discovered the security vulnerability, he immediately restricted access to the staging environment. Then he and his team started a review of other development and test environments in the company to make sure none of them was open to exploitation. The takeaway here is as accessible as that SQL file: Don't get lax with security simply because an environment is made for testing. Even if the test server was live for only a day, that’s a day where it could be exploited. “The incident completely changed how I look at staging environments. If an environment has access to real data, it needs to be treated as a real security asset — regardless of whether the developers expect it to exist for a day, a week, or six months,” Schut said.®

entries.title: 借助 GPT Astra，开发者实现在《我的世界》中原生运行《使命召唤：黑色行动 2》
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 17 日消息，一位热衷于人工智能和游戏开发的开发者近日展示了一个有趣的项目：经典射击游戏《使命召唤：黑色行动 2》（Call of Duty: Black Ops 2）的“Hijacked”地图如今可以原生运行在《我的世界》中。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/907a0027-1b0e-4326-af55-5123fe5c5b8a.jpg?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

IT之家注意到，Luckey Faraday 在 X（原 Twitter）发文介绍称，他们此前曾制作过一个基于浏览器运行的《黑色行动 2》移植版本。最初，他们将这套程序嵌入《我的世界》，让游戏以“游戏内一台电脑屏幕”的形式运行。随后，Faraday 使用 GPT Astra 重构了整个项目，使“Hijacked”地图能够“直接运行在《我的世界》自身的 OpenGL 上下文中”。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/9122e06c-22d5-47aa-b713-57a49abc156c.png?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

从公开的视频来看，这张发布于 2012 年的《使命召唤》经典地图如今可以在《我的世界》中以全屏方式运行，整体运行较为流畅，帧率约为 45 FPS。

Faraday 介绍称：“地图、碰撞检测、机器人、导航网格、武器以及渲染，全部都作为 Fabric 模组运行在《我的世界》内部。”

Fabric 是一款轻量级、开源的《我的世界》模组加载器和开发 API。因此，这次移植并不是简单地在《我的世界》中播放《黑色行动 2》的画面，而是通过 Fabric 模组框架，将《黑色行动 2》的相关内容以及“Hijacked”地图直接注入《我的世界》。

Faraday 运营着一个 AI 开发者社区，邀请其他爱好者共同制作演示项目，并分享开发日志和代码。这次移植项目也很好地体现了他们的开发流程。

具体来看，开发者最初先让“Hijacked”地图能够在浏览器中运行。随后，他们又将这一版本“硬塞”进《我的世界》，但当时它实际上只是作为一个独立游戏运行在沙盒游戏中的“一台电脑”里。之后，Faraday 决定让 GPT Astra 使用 Java 重新构建整个项目。借助重写后的代码，他们最终实现了让这款经典 FPS 地图直接运行在《我的世界》的 OpenGL 上下文中。

Faraday 表示，目前项目“还有很多工作要做”。不过从目前的演示来看，这张以豪华游艇为场景的紧凑地图已经具备相当程度的可玩性，并非只是简单地在《我的世界》中展示画面。如果项目继续推进，未来或许还会加入更多地图、武器以及多人游戏模式。

《我的世界》是全球销量最高的电子游戏之一。这款游戏凭借冒险、创造建筑以及社交玩法吸引了大量年轻玩家，其高度开放和可扩展的沙盒架构同样吸引了许多技术能力出众的开发者。这也使《我的世界》成为各种令人惊叹的计算机科学实验的载体。例如，此前就有人将一个拥有约 500 万参数、可以实际运行的 ChatGPT 模型塞进《我的世界》，并将其命名为 CraftGPT。

entries.title: OpenAI 最新报告：企业员工用上 AI 后，逐渐开始处理本职范围外的任务
entries.content:
IT之家 9 月 17 日消息，当地时间 16 日，OpenAI 发布的最新《工作前沿》报告显示，企业能否真正用好 AI，不只取决于员工有没有 AI 工具，也取决于**工作本身如何拆分和安排**。

员工借助 AI 处理本职范围之外的任务后，其中一些任务会逐渐进入日常工作流程。如果这些活动最终变成固定职责，即使职位名称没有变化，**实际工作内容也可能越来越宽**。

OpenAI 曾在首份《工作前沿》报告提出了“任务跨界”现象：员工借助 AI 处理过去**通常属于其他职业的工作**。最新研究则进一步追问，这种跨界尝试之后**会发生什么**。

据IT之家了解，这项研究为期 4 个月、针对专业岗位员工 AI 使用方式和提示词，分析了 2026 年 4 月至 7 月超过 150 万条工作类 ChatGPT 消息，结果显示，一部分跨职业 AI 使用并非一次性尝试。员工会反复处理超出自身职业边界的任务，而且时间越长，这类活动在其 AI 使用中的占比越高。

这些发现初步揭示了一个变化过程：员工获得 AI 工具后，**或会****先尝试处理新的任务，随后再把其中一部分纳入固定工作习惯**。对于仍在摸索如何在组织内部部署和使用 AI 的企业而言，研究为理解 AI 如何缩短**“发现问题”与“真正推动工作向前”**之间的距离提供了重要线索。研究也表明，企业制定 AI 战略时，不能只考虑给员工提供什么工具，还需要重新考虑工作本身该如何设计。

员工面对本职范围内和范围外的任务时，使用 AI 的方式并不一样。处理原有职责之外的工作时，员工平均输入的提示词更短，也较少要求 AI 解释原理、提供操作步骤、按照指定格式回答或给出建议。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2024/10/1e49cd7b-4b1b-4d78-b322-580914f2f7fa.png?x-bce-process=image/watermark,text_QUnnlJ_miJA,type_RlpMYW5UaW5nSGVpU0JHQg==,size_23,color_ffffffdd,skw_1,skc_00000051,g_7,blr_50,bls_50,x_9,y_9)

不过，在处理本职范围之外的任务时，**员工更愿意向 AI 提供示例和背景，也更常要求 AI 帮忙检查或验证**。

一种可能的解释是，员工把 AI 当成了“借用其他专业能力”的工具。他们并不一定希望 AI 从头教会自己一个陌生领域，而是往往带着具体问题和必要材料，例如文件、示例或同事提供的信息，再让 AI 帮助调用另一个领域的知识解决问题。

研究持续追踪了 2026 年 4 月至 7 月约 6200 名员工。员工此前处理过的跨职业任务，占具体职业类 AI 活动的比例**从 4 月的 13.1% 升至 7 月的 25.9%**。这说明，一部分跨界任务并没有停留在尝鲜阶段，而是逐渐进入日常工作流程。

另一组数据进一步说明了这种变化。在抽样的一月期匹配追踪中，员工次月再次处理上个月某项跨职业任务的比例达到 23.6%；对于此前一个月没有处理过同一任务的可比员工，这一比例只有 8.4%。本职范围内任务和通用任务也呈现出类似差距。

不同工作的“留存率”差别很大。以下几类跨职业任务，员工在次月继续处理的比例相对较高：

* 与客户讨论商品或服务：54%
* 撰写广告或推广文案：44%
* 制作营销材料：37%

相比之下，“解释财务信息”的次月重复使用率约为 15%，而所有跨职业任务的平均水平为 18.5%。这种差异可能说明，有些工作天然更容易融入 AI 工作流程，也可能与企业内部规范、员工谨慎程度，以及做错之后可能带来的后果有关。

报告认为，由此可以看到一种可能的 AI 职位演变路径：**员工先尝试处理传统职责之外的任务，发现 AI 能够帮上忙，随后开始在日常工作中不断回到这项任务。**

参考

* <https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/work-at-the-frontier-report-202609.pdf>

entries.title: A20 Pro succeeds because it was built just for what Apple needs
entries.content:
Apple executives have been talking in detail about the [iPhone 18 Pro's](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone-18 "iPhone 18") 2nm A20 Pro processor, but also how it was intentionally designed alongside so many other elements to provide greater speed and efficiency.  
  

![Middleaged man speaking while seated in a chair, gesturing with both hands, with a glowing Apple A20 Pro processor logo displayed beside him on a dark background](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/69023-145528-000-lead-Sri-Santhanam-d3-xl.jpg)  
Sri Santhanam talks about the design of the A20 Pro processor - image credit: The Circuit podcast

  
The A20 Pro processor in the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and [iPhone Duo](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone-duo "iPhone Duo") is the [most capable chip](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/09/10/siri-ai-is-so-close-to-being-useful-and-iphone-duos-a20-pro-could-be-the-secret-sauce) ever in any [iPhone](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone "iPhone"). Each generation is of course better than the last, but this is the first to be made to a 2-nanometer design, and the result is a 20% faster CPU and 40% faster GPU.  
  
Apple chiefs, though, say that the 2nm processor is only part of what has been done to make the new iPhones perform better, stay cooler, and be better suited for AI work. Speaking on "The Circuit" [podcast](https://finance.biggo.com/podcast/e069c38541099118), [Apple Silicon](https://appleinsider.com/inside/apple-silicon "Apple Silicon") and product marketing chiefs Tom Boger, Kaiann Drance, and Sri Santhanam also detailed the side-mounted DRAM, the MCM-style packaging, and the increased neural engine count as key to the new processor.  
  
  
 [Continue Reading on AppleInsider](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/09/17/a20-pro-succeeds-because-it-was-built-just-for-what-apple-needs?utm_source=rss) | [Discuss on our Forums](https://forums.appleinsider.com/discussion/245709?urm_source=rss)
entries.summary: 苹果芯片高管详述2nm A20 Pro处理器的架构定制与AI计算效率提升。

entries.title: This Two-Year Proton VPN Plan With Unlimited Bandwidth Is 70% Off Right Now
entries.content:
Deal pricing and availability subject to change after time of publication.

Proton VPN’s latest promotion offers its [two-year VPN Plus plan](https://go.linkby.com/NIWMTIJB "open in a new window") for $2.99 per month (down from $9.99), a 70% discount that saves you $168 over the introductory term. While the monthly figure is useful for comparison, this is not a month-to-month subscription: Proton charges the full $71.76 when you sign up—though you do get a 30-day money-back guarantee, giving you time to check how it performs with your devices, internet connection, and streaming services. After the initial 24 months, the plan renews at $83.88 per year, or $6.99 per month.

For everyday use, you can open the app and let Proton pick a server, or choose from more than 140 countries when you need a particular location. That could help you access services from home while traveling, although streaming platforms may still block VPN connections. The subscription also covers 10 devices at once (so there’s room for your phone, laptop, and TV without switching between them), with apps for Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, and supported TV devices, including Fire TV. Whatever device you use, there’s no bandwidth cap to keep track of, though the speed depends on your connection and which of Proton’s 20,000-plus servers you choose—its VPN Accelerator may help, but the advertised improvement of up to 400% applies to VPN connections, and it shouldn’t be read as a promise to quadruple your broadband speed.

Beyond changing your apparent location, privacy is the stronger reason to consider Proton, whose apps are open-source and independently audited, with a [published external audit of its no-logs policy](https://protonvpn.com/blog/no-logs-audit "open in a new window") offering more accountability than a blanket promise of anonymity—but those checks, while useful, won’t stop a website from recognizing you when you sign in. For extra protection (at the possible expense of speed), you can also enable [Secure Core](https://protonvpn.com/features/secure-core "open in a new window"), which sends traffic through an additional server in places such as Switzerland or Iceland. Meanwhile, [NetShield](https://protonvpn.com/support/netshield "open in a new window") blocks known ad, tracking, and malware domains, helping prevent some unwanted resources from loading without guaranteeing ad-free streaming or protection against every threat. Taken together, all these features make the subscription, at this introductory price, worth considering if you use VPN regularly across several devices.

*An advertiser paid for editorial consideration of this deal. Our editorial experts vetted the deal based on our independent expertise. Because we determined that the deal will save money for the consumer, we wrote the content.*

entries.title: More iPhone price hikes loom as Apple reportedly accepts brutal memory deal
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

Apple products have never been thought of as a budget option, but this year has been particularly rough for fans on a budget. The situation can be traced to the rise of AI, as datacenters hoover up the available memory chips, pushing up wholesale prices and leading manufacturers to pass on these extra costs to the consumer.

For a while, Apple customers were largely unaffected, but in June the company ramped up the price of all Macs and iPads [by at least $100](https://www.macworld.com/article/3176418/ugh-apples-price-hikes-are-brutal.html) (and in one case by as much as $1,300). Then earlier this month it did something similar [to its iPhones](https://www.macworld.com/article/3229342/iphone-price-increases.html), adding anywhere from $100 to $500 across the range. The high price of memory is also a factor in the high initial pricing of the iPhone Duo, which starts at $1,999.

And the pain isn’t over just yet. Earlier this week, the Twitter/X leaker [Semiconductor Insider](https://x.com/SemiconductorsX/status/2099696524771143964) (via [AppleInsider](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/09/16/dram-pricing-will-mean-more-iphone-price-hikes-in-2027-no-relief-through-2028)) discussed a new quote Samsung had given Apple to supply memory in the first quarter of 2027, and the figures make for ominous reading. The prices–DRAM at around $2 per Gb, and NAND at $0.33 per Gb–are 30-40 percent up on current rates. That’s a big hike in manufacturing costs, and Apple will be reluctant to take the hit and reduce its profit margins. In other words, we can expect further iPhone price rises in 2027.

At that stage, it wasn’t clear if Apple would sign the deal, but [DigiTimes](https://www.digitimes.com/news/a20260916VL210/apple-samsung-2027-smartphone-cost.html) reported Wednesday that Apple had indeed accepted the higher costs. DigiTimes has a weak track record for Apple rumors, but it’s much more reliable for industry deals.

We don’t know if Apple will increase the starting prices of the new iPhones as a result of the supplier deal, but the situation will certainly create complications in the spring. This month’s iPhone event was all about the [unobtainable luxuries](https://www.macworld.com/article/3228624/apples-surprise-event-was-a-parade-of-unobtainable-luxuries.html), but we’re due to get more budget-focused handsets in March or April: the iPhone 18 and the iPhone 18e (plus the iPhone Air 2, potentially, but that won’t be cheap). It’ll be tough to market the iPhone 18e as a budget option if it gets another price hike and starts at $799.

If all this makes you think about jumping ship and getting an Android device instead, it’s worth bearing in mind that other manufacturers face the same issues and may suffer more. As Semiconductor Insider points out, Apple’s deal “is the price floor for everyone else.” The Cupertino company has immense leverage and almost always gets the best supplier deals. Whatever it’s paying, Android companies will have to pay the same or more.

entries.title: Apple Watch Ultra 4 Review: The smartwatch for the health-conscious
entries.content:
![Apple Watch Ultra 4](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/00umeK58AfBDF7MEJ8I7xUJ/hero-image.jpg)

This is going to be a review in progress. The reason is simple: the new [Apple Watch Ultra 4](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-watch-ultra-4-announcement-iphone-event-2026), unveiled last week and launching properly tomorrow, touts numerous new features that won't be available until later this year (if you're in Europe, the timeline is unknown).

[Apple](https://mashable.com/category/apple) provided me with a review unit of the new Ultra 4, and all I could do was focus on what was there. The highlights: longer battery life (huge!) and a new heart rate monitoring system, which Apple says is best in the business.

First, the specs:

* **Case**: Titanium
* **Colors**: Natural or Black
* **Case size**: 49mm
* **Display resolution**: 422x514 pixels, 1,245 square mm display area
* **Display brightness**: Up to 3,000 nits peak brightness, 1 nit minimum brightness
* **Display type**: Wide-angle OLED and LTPO3
* **Chip**: S11 with a 4-core Neural Engine, W3 wireless chip
* **Storage**: 64GB
* **Connectivity**: GPS, Cellular (5G and LTE), WiFi4, Bluetooth 5.3, satellite connectivity, second-gen Ultra Wideband chip
* **Battery life**: up to 50 hours of normal use, up to 84 hours in Low Power Mode
* **Charging**: Up to 80 percent charge in about 45 minutes
* **Durability**: Water resistance 100m, recreational scuba diving to 40m, dust resistance IP6X, tested to MIL-STD 810H standard
* **Special features**: Second-generation electrical heart sensor, always-on optical heart sensor

## So what's new here?

![Apple Watch Ultra 4](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/00umeK58AfBDF7MEJ8I7xUJ/images-1.fill.size_2000x1436.v1789637035.jpg)

Apple Watch Ultra 4 repeats the colors from last year: Black Titanium (pictured) and Natural Titanium.
Credit: Stan Schroeder/Mashable

If you take a closer look at those specs and compare them to the [Ultra Watch 3](https://mashable.com/article/apple-watch-ultra-3-versus-ultra-2), you'll see they're almost identical, with the only differences being the new chip, better battery life, and the second-gen heart-monitoring system. That's right: Even the colors are the same as last year and boil down to Natural Titanium or Black Titanium (my unit was of the Natural Titanium variety).

This is the rare gadget where I don't really mind the lack of visual updates. The Apple Watch Ultra has looked pretty much the same since the first version, but it looks rugged, powerful, and mighty, with a beautiful display that puts most other smartwatches to shame. I wouldn't mind a new case color just for variety's sake, but the design is (still) great.

It does, however, mean that I have little to report on display size, brightness, or basic functionality. It's all the same as last year's version.

![Apple Watch Ultra 4](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/00umeK58AfBDF7MEJ8I7xUJ/images-6.fill.size_2000x1556.v1789637598.jpg)

The Siri Modular Watch Face has a special complication in the middle that always surfaces the most relevant widget. 
Credit: Stan Schroeder/Mashable

As for new watch faces, Apple's new [watchOS 27](https://mashable.com/category/apple-watch) (which is what my unit is running) brings only one: Siri Modular. It's available for both the [Series 12 and Ultra 4](https://mashable.com/tech/apple-watch-series-12-ultra-4-preorder-price-release-date), but thanks to the Ultra 4's larger display, it has an additional bezel and a different (optional) Ultra font.

The new trick Siri Modular does is dynamically change the center complication to display whatever the top Smart Stack widget is at the moment. Turn the Watch's crown, and that widget will start rotating between the other widgets in your smart stack.

While the new Siri Modular face is a cool addition, I do regret that Apple didn't add additional new faces with the launch of the Watch Ultra 4. While its physical design remains the same, new watch faces are the easiest way to make the watch feel fresh.

![Apple Watch Ultra 4](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/00umeK58AfBDF7MEJ8I7xUJ/images-5.fill.size_2000x1349.v1789637036.jpg)

I'm sticking with the Translucent Gray Ocean Band. 
Credit: Stan Schroeder/Mashable

One fresh thing is the wide range of bands on offer. Apple added numerous new versions across all of its band types, including Sport Band, Sport Loop, Nike Sport Band, and Hermes. Apple sent me a few to try out; by far my favorite was the new Translucent Gray Ocean Band, which is a perfect match for the Apple Watch Ultra 4's Natural Titanium color.

## Battery life fit for athletes

The Apple Watch Ultra has always been advertised as a watch for athletes and adventurers, but the first couple of iterations just didn't have the battery life to match that claim. Now, with the Apple Watch Ultra 4, Apple says the battery will last up to 50 hours in normal use, up to 84 hours in Low Power Mode, and up to 18 hours in outdoor workout mode.

This should now be enough to finish an Ironman race, which is pretty much all you can ask of any sports watch. I haven't tried that and have no plans to, but I did take the Watch for an hour-long workout that included some calisthenics and bag work. The watch was fully charged that morning, and by evening it still had 81 percent battery remaining.

Overall, I had to charge the Watch roughly every third day, and could extend that by another day by using low power mode. This is a big deal for me as it means I don't have to worry about charging when I take the Watch on a weekend trip.

## New heart rate monitoring system

The biggest hardware change on both the Watch Ultra 4 and Apple Watch Series 12 is the completely new Health Sensing System, which includes a new optical and electrical heart sensor. It can take heart rate measurements far more frequently throughout the day, thereby collecting more data, which is used to calculate metrics such as HRV (heart rate variability), a stress indicator. Apple pointed to a scientific [study](https://www.apple.com/health/pdf/Heart_Rate_Accuracy_Study_2026.pdf) that singles out this new system as the best among wearables right now.

![Apple Watch Ultra 4](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/00umeK58AfBDF7MEJ8I7xUJ/images-2.fill.size_2000x1349.v1789637035.jpg)

The new heart rate monitoring system takes measurements far more frequently than before. 
Credit: Stan Schroeder/Mashable

This new system also paved the way for Readiness, a feature that takes a bunch of data and essentially tells you how well you're doing and how ready you are to tackle a workout. Readiness takes a week of data to start showing up; I don't have a score yet, but will add it here as soon as I get that first reading.

Other health-related apps, such as Vitals and Heart Rate, now provide more precise, granular data thanks to the new heart rate monitoring system. One metric I find particularly useful is the ability to see at a glance how quickly your heart rate returns to normal after a hard workout.

The new heart rate monitoring sensors do fire more often, which can be a nuisance while you sleep or in a dark theater. Apple has thought of this, and the sensors will fire less often when the watch is in Theater or Sleep Focus mode.

![Apple Watch Ultra 4](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/00umeK58AfBDF7MEJ8I7xUJ/images-4.fill.size_2000x1250.v1789637036.jpg)

In a dark room, the constant flickering of the heart rate sensors can be annoying, but fortunately there are ways to temporarily (and automatically) turn it off. 
Credit: Stan Schroeder/Mashable

Step tracking has also been improved, with Apple calling it "the most accurate in any smartwatch." I've been getting slightly lower step counts than on the Apple Watch Series 11, but it's hard to say whether that's more accurate than before. I have, however, enjoyed the new Steps complication, which shows me the number of steps I've taken today in real-time.

## The stuff that's not here yet

Now we come to the complicated part. The new Apple Watch Ultra 4, as well as Series 12, come with several AI features. These are part of the Audio Intelligence suite of features, enabled by the new S11 chip, which includes four new features: improved Shazam, Sound Recognition, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap.

Shazam, which comes in the form of the Music Recognition widget, is simply better at identifying the song playing nearby. I've tried it out on numerous songs, even some obscure YouTube remixes, and it recognized them all instantly.

Sound Recognition is primarily aimed at people with hearing impairments, as it can help them recognize important sounds such as sirens, doorbells, or a baby crying.

![Apple Watch Ultra 4](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/00umeK58AfBDF7MEJ8I7xUJ/images-7.fill.size_2000x1512.v1789637598.jpg)

Music Recognition now works incredibly fast, and I couldn't find a song it couldn't recognize. 
Credit: Stan Schroeder/Mashable

Those two are live now, but Live Rewind and Siri Recap are coming "later this year." Live Rewind gives you an AI-powered recap of the last 15 seconds of your life, so you can recall, for example, which menu items the restaurant waiter just listed for you. Siri Recap creates a "high-level summary" of your day.

Apple has pointed out that these don't store any audio data and are completely private to the user, but they still sound like potential privacy trouble to me. The features are opt-in to you, the user, but they listen to everyone around you, and these people may not always get a chance to opt in or out. Live Rewind does, however, play an audible sound, even if the Watch is on silent, and displays an animation, so that people nearby can see that it's being used.

We'll know more about these features when they go live. In Europe, where the privacy rules are pretty strict, it might take a while.

All of the health and fitness data collected by the Watch feeds into the Health app on the iPhone, which has undergone a big redesign. That, however, also isn't live yet; as I wrap up this text, it just became available in the iOS 27 developer beta. At first glance, I think the new Health app is a huge improvement, as it offers a clearer overview of various aspects of your health, including sleep quality, fitness level, heart health, and overall vital signs. I'll need more time (and a more finalized version) to assess how well it works, though.

## Should you buy it?

![Apple Watch Ultra 4](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/reviews/00umeK58AfBDF7MEJ8I7xUJ/images-3.fill.size_2000x1184.v1789637036.jpg)

It's an amazing smartwatch, but not an essential upgrade from last year's model. 
Credit: Stan Schroeder/Mashable

Whether you need the new Apple Watch Ultra 4 depends on how you use it. If it's just a cool watch on your wrist that you sometimes use for workouts, and you don't require very precise sports metrics, then the old Ultra 3 or even Ultra 2 will continue to serve you well.

If you're an athlete, especially an endurance athlete, who needs the best battery life and the best heart rate measurement system available, then the Apple Watch Ultra 4 is an essential upgrade, even if you have an older version.

entries.title: NightmareStresser Goes Offline in Global DDoS-for-Hire Crackdown
entries.content:
## The DOJ seized domains behind NightmareStresser, a DDoS-for-hire service tied to hundreds of thousands of attacks since 2022, as part of Operation PowerOFF.

Renting a DDoS attack used to be as easy as renting a movie. Pick a target, pay a few dollars, watch the site go dark. The Justice Department just made that a little harder by seizing the domains behind NightmareStresser, one of the longest-running services in that business.

*“The Justice Department today announced the court-authorized seizure of internet domains associated with one of the world’s longest running Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) for-hire services known as “NightmareStresser.” ” [states DoJ](https://www.justice.gov/usao-ak/pr/fbi-seizes-ddos-hire-domains-part-continuing-district-alaska-crackdown-booter-and).*

*“Federal law enforcement has seized websites maintained by criminal service providers that allow paying customers to launch powerful DDoS attacks targeting victims in the District of Alaska and worldwide as part of coordinated actions to disrupt so called “Booter” or “Stresser” operators.”*

The announcement came from the District of Alaska, which may seem like an unusual place for a DDoS takedown. But Anchorage prosecutors have been investigating and fighting DDoS-for-hire services for almost a decade.

Federal authorities seized the websites under a court-approved warrant, preventing customers from using the service to launch attacks against targets in Alaska and around the world. These services are often called “booters” or “stressers,” names that make renting a DDoS attack sound like a simple online service.

It’s tempting to file DDoS attacks under “annoying but harmless.” The DOJ’s own description of the victim pool argues otherwise.

*“Booter services such as those named in this action allegedly facilitate attacks on a wide array of victims in the United States and abroad, including educational institutions, government agencies, gaming platforms and millions of people. In addition to affecting targeted victims, these attacks can significantly degrade internet services and can completely disrupt internet connections.” continues DoJ. “According to the seizure warrant affidavit, the NightmareStresser Booter service targeted in this operation was used to launch hundreds of thousands of actual or attempted DDoS attacks targeting victims worldwide since 2022. “*

A school district losing internet access during exam week, a city government portal going dark, a gaming server getting flooded mid-match: none of that is abstract to the people dealing with it in the moment.

These attacks can slow down internet services or completely take them offline. The impact can also go beyond the main target, affecting other users and services that rely on the same network infrastructure.

NightmareStresser wasn’t a small operation running a handful of scripts for hobbyists.

*“According to the seizure warrant affidavit, the NightmareStresser Booter service targeted in this operation was used to launch hundreds of thousands of actual or attempted DDoS attacks targeting victims worldwide since 2022.” states DoJ.*

That’s over three years of near-continuous rental attacks, on a service that markets itself with a name straight out of a horror movie.

The FBI’s Anchorage Field Office ran the technical side with help from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police’s Federal Policing Northwest Region. It’s a reminder that DDoS-for-hire crime doesn’t respect borders, so neither does the response to it.

This seizure sits inside [Operation PowerOFF](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/operation-poweroff), the ongoing international campaign that’s been dismantling DDoS-for-hire infrastructure and going after the people running it for years. Just this past April, a coordinated action across 21 countries took down 53 domains, arrested four operators, and sent warning letters to more than 75,000 identified users of these platforms. Before that, in December 2024, another PowerOFF sweep knocked out 27 booter sites in one go.

Alaska’s own contribution to that broader effort goes back further than most people would guess.

*“In previous law enforcement actions involving prosecutors and investigators in Anchorage and Los Angeles over the last eight years, the Justice Department charged twelve defendants who facilitated DDoS-for hire services and seized more than 100 internet domains associated with DDoS-for-hire services.” continues DoJ. “The multi-prong investigation announced today builds on the success of the prior cases by targeting all known booter sites, shutting down as many as possible, and undertaking a public education campaign.”*

Twelve people and a hundred domains later, they’re still finding new ones to shut down.

Booter services are difficult to eliminate completely. When one is taken down, another can quickly appear, often using similar business models. The DOJ says these services have continued to grow because they make it easy for people with little technical knowledge to launch DDoS attacks.

Users don’t need to write code or understand how networks work. They can simply visit a website, pay for the service, often using cryptocurrency, and choose their target. This low barrier to entry has made DDoS-for-hire services accessible to a much wider group of cybercriminals.

Assistant U.S. Attorneys Adam Alexander and Ainsley McNerney are prosecuting the case out of the District of Alaska. The DOJ was explicit that this investigation isn’t a one-off strike but part of a wider plan to target every known booter site it can find, shut down as many as possible, and keep running public education alongside the legal action.

**Follow me on Twitter:**[**@securityaffairs**](https://twitter.com/securityaffairs)**and**[**Facebook**](https://www.facebook.com/sec.affairs)**and**[**Mastodon**](https://infosec.exchange/@securityaffairs)

[**Pierluigi Paganini**](http://www.linkedin.com/pub/pierluigi-paganini/b/742/559)

**(**[**SecurityAffairs**](http://securityaffairs.co/wordpress/)**– hacking, Operation PowerOFF)**

entries.title: Cisco drops another exploited zero-day, this time a perfect 10
entries.content: Cisco admins who have spent their week patching email gateways now face a perfect-10 Identity Services Engine flaw under active attack. Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76460 on Wednesday, describing it as an authentication bypass affecting Identity Services Engine (ISE) and ISE Passive Identity Connector (ISE-PIC). Successful exploitation can give an unauthenticated remote attacker command execution with root privileges. Product Security Incident Response Team said it was aware of active exploitation and urged customers to install the fixes immediately. CISA has also added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The warning follows another actively exploited critical vulnerability disclosed days earlier, CVE-2026-76461, affecting its Secure Email Gateway and Secure Email and Web Manager appliances. That 9.8-rated bug could also lead to root access, prompting Cisco to warn admins that attackers may be able to cover their tracks after getting in. The latest problem lies in an API within Cisco ISE, the company's network access control platform. Cisco says insufficient authentication controls on an API endpoint mean an attacker can send a crafted request to bypass the product's web-based management interface. No credentials or user interaction are required, and Cisco says vulnerable versions of ISE and ISE-PIC are affected regardless of configuration. The flaw received the maximum CVSS score of 10.0. Cisco warned that root access could allow attackers to remove or conceal traces of an intrusion, complicating efforts to determine whether an appliance had been breached. Cisco advised admins to review ISE access logs for suspicious usernames on every node in a distributed deployment and to check network and firewall logs held outside the affected device for signs of unexpected uploads or downloads. If admins find evidence of possible exploitation, Cisco "strongly recommends" reimaging affected nodes and restoring their configurations from backup if necessary. No workaround exists, although Cisco said infrastructure access control lists can be used as a temporary mitigation to restrict management and control-plane traffic reaching affected systems. Permanent fixes are available in ISE and ISE-PIC 3.1 Patch 12, 3.2 Patch 11, 3.3 Patch 12, 3.4 Patch 7 and 3.5 Patch 4. ISE 3.0 has reached the end of software maintenance, so customers running it must migrate to a supported release. Cisco discovered CVE-2026-76460 while resolving a Technical Assistance Center support case, but has not disclosed who is exploiting it, how long the attacks have been underway, or what the intruders have done after gaining access. The advisory accompanied a substantial batch of other ISE vulnerabilities published Wednesday. Two other Cisco advisories carried maximum CVSS scores of 10.0, while a separate trio of remote code execution flaws scored as high as 9.9. For admins responsible for Cisco kit, September is shaping up to be quite the patching month. ®
