entries.title: Cute Critters Come to the Cloud: ‘Aniimo’ Launches on GeForce NOW
entries.content:
A new creature-catching adventure is ready to stream from the cloud this week. Pawprint Studio’s *Aniimo* arrives on [GeForce NOW](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/?ncid=pa-srch-goog-673352&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=24109411186&gbraid=0AAAAAD4XAoFU8ggWk_ctIMbhcvIsRyJpn&gclid=Cj0KCQjwh4TVBhCWARIsAG0czmpnuXeOukbuTNygy2VzBtR3O7EIei492KMT7sDRCIKviJ0yAbJtl_saAl6AEALw_wcB) at launch, inviting gamers to explore the vibrant continent of Idyll across supported devices.

Also this week, *007 First Light* receives a path-tracing update on GeForce NOW, alongside a smashing limited-time Deluxe Edition sale on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3768760/007_First_Light/) and [Epic Games Store](https://store.epicgames.com/p/007-first-light-182cea?lang=en-US).

Gaijin Network’s fractured-multiverse action game *Active Matter* and Annapurna Interactive’s acclaimed space mystery *Outer Wilds* are also among 11 new titles [joining the cloud](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/games/) this week.

## **Explore Idyll With the Cutest Companions**

The path to Idyll begins now. *Aniimo* is a free-to-play, open-world creature-catching role-playing game where every creature encountered can become a companion. Catch Aniimo with Aniipods, then Twine with them to take on their form and use unique skills to solve puzzles, win battles and overcome challenges.

Glide, dive and burrow across Idyll, then return to a personal RV to build a warm, interactive Homeland alongside Aniimo companions. Stream Aniimo on a [Steam Deck](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-steam-deck-geforce-now/), in the newly supported [Firefox browser](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/geforce-now-thursday-firefox/) and across any other supported devices — without waiting through its 45GB download or making room in local storage. There’s always room in the Homeland for one more Aniimo.

## **Choose Your Path**

[![007 First Light on GeForce NOW](https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/007_First_Light_GeForce_NOW_September_17_2026-1680x840.jpg)](https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/007_First_Light_GeForce_NOW_September_17_2026.jpg)

Licensed to render.

In the critically acclaimed, multimillion-selling [*007 First Light*](https://ioi.dk/007firstlightgame), follow James Bond as a young, resourceful and sometimes reckless recruit in MI6’s training program, and discover a reimagined origin story of the world’s most famous spy. Incorporating IO Interactive’s signature stealth gameplay with world-class Bond action, players can embark on missions in breathtaking locations around the globe, drive iconic vehicles and dive into a cinematic adventure in pursuit of a rogue agent who’s always one step ahead.

Path tracing has now [been added](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce/news/007-first-light-path-tracing-dlss-4-5-ray-reconstruction-update-out-now/) to *007 First Light*, introducing extra-detailed lighting, shadows and reflections, making its levels and set pieces even more cinematic, immersive and realistic. And NVIDIA DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction ensures the fidelity, clarity and accuracy of these additions are at their absolute best.

[Ultimate members](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/premium-memberships/) can stream with GeForce RTX 5080-class performance, with up to 5K high dynamic range and cinematic-quality streaming. DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution and Dynamic Frame Generation accelerate frame rates and enhance image quality.

A limited-time opportunity awaits: the *007 First Light Deluxe Edition* is on sale on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3768760/007_First_Light/) from Sept. 15-29 and on [Epic Games Store](https://store.epicgames.com/p/007-first-light-182cea?lang=en-US) from Sept. 3-18. The mission is on sale. The getaway car is in the cloud.

## **Matter of Time**

Gaijin’s *Active Matter*, a realistic military shooter set in a fractured multiverse, has launched on GeForce NOW. As an operative stuck in a time loop, join dangerous raids for loot or intense player vs. player battles.

Fight against rivals from other timelines, survive physics-breaking anomalies and try to stay alive. Harvest active matter, gather loot and extract to a safe place before the whole zone ceases to exist.

Ultimate members can take on each raid with GeForce RTX 5080-class performance in the cloud, delivering high frame rates, advanced graphics features and low latency across supported devices. The zone won’t wait — and neither does the next loop.

## **Let’s Get Loopy**

[![Outer Wilds on GeForce NOW](https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Outer_Wilds_GeForce_NOW_September_17_2026-1680x840.jpg)](https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Outer_Wilds_GeForce_NOW_September_17_2026.jpg)

Every loop holds another secret.

*Outer Wilds* joins the GeForce NOW library this week. As the newest recruit of Outer Wilds Ventures, search for answers across a strange, ever-changing solar system trapped in an endless time loop. Gamers can trace mysterious signals, decipher alien writing and discover hidden locations before an underground city is swallowed by sand or a planet crumbles beneath their feet.

There’s even more to stream this week:

* *Active Matter* (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2887580/Active_Matter/) and [Gaijin](https://activematter.game/?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Sept. 15)
* *Aniimo* (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4126040/Aniimo/), Sept. 15)
* *RuneScape: Dragonwilds* (New release on [Xbox](https://www.xbox.com/games/store/runescape-dragonwilds/9p402rwr63h4?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now), Sept. 15, available on Game Pass)
* *Train Sim World 7* (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4678800/Train_Sim_World_7/), Sept. 15)
* *The Guild 1 Remake: Europa 1410* (New release on [Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2977260/The_Guild_1_Remake_Europa_1410/), Sept. 17)
* *The Blood of Dawnwalker* ([GOG.com](https://www.gog.com/game/the_blood_of_dawnwalker?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now))
* *Mixtape* ([Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/2582320?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now))
* *Neon White* ([Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1533420?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now))

* *What Remains of Edith Finch* ([Steam](https://store.steampowered.com/app/501300?utm_source=nvidia&utm_campaign=geforce_now))

Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after they’re released and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates to announced titles.

Ready to take this week’s new games for a spin? Start with a [day pass](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/geforce-now/?ncid=pa-srch-goog-673352&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=24109411186&gbraid=0AAAAAD4XAoGPVGKakiCteqkRtoF1Q-KSI&gclid=CjwKCAjws_DTBhB_EiwAXZknGUBjXpM5vNQvnwLXUGilFsIHBSkbKPfllg7RGpFFuQZv2GFityJC6BoCq8MQAvD_BwE) to try premium cloud gaming before committing to a membership. Even better, the cost of the day pass can be applied toward a first monthly membership — making it easy to level up with GeForce RTX-powered cloud gaming.

IT之家 9 月 17 日消息，据外媒 Eurogamer 今天（17 日）晚间报道，《战狗》现已跻身今年 Steam 最热门的 PC 游戏之列。最新数据显示，其发售表现甚至超过《ARC Raiders》和《绝地潜兵 2》等热门作品，与表现不佳的《失落星船：马拉松》相比差距更加明显。

![](https://img.ithome.com/newsuploadfiles/2026/9/340482be-53e0-4bc4-b655-2ce34f407e32.png?x-bce-process=image/format,f_auto)

Alinea Analytics 分析师里斯 · 埃利奥特称，《战狗》目前**累计销量超过 220 万份**。把几款游戏在 Steam 发售后的同期表现放在一起比较，《ARC Raiders》卖出 170 万份，《绝地潜兵 2》为 100 万份，《战狗》的销售速度明显更快。

埃利奥特透露，**《战狗》目前只登陆 Steam，收入却超过了《失落星船：马拉松》全平台总和**。《战狗》累计收入达到 7,000 万美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 4.71 亿元人民币），按收入计算，在 Steam 2026 年新游戏榜单中位列第 7。游戏也计划登陆 PlayStation 和 Xbox，不过主机版要到 2028 年才会推出。

埃利奥特指出，《战狗》正好找到了当下游戏市场的定价“甜蜜点”，既避开了 70 美元（现汇率约合 470.6 元人民币）3A 游戏带来的消费门槛，又吸引了大量买不起高价游戏的玩家。

埃利奥特的分析还显示，《战狗》有 11% 的 Steam 愿望单最终转化为购买，而全部愿望单中有 57% 都是过去一个月新增的。

entries.title: The Liftoff Scenario That Terrifies A.I. Doomsayers - The New York Times
entries.content: “Recursive self-improvement” is the idea that artificial intelligence could learn to build and train itself, creating exponential new progress — and risk. Their goal: to build an A.I. system smart enough to build a better A.I. system. Named for the 19th-century English physicist Michael Faraday, it gathers mountains of data capturing the daily activities of Dr. Hughes, Dr. Kirsch and Inherent’s other researchers: emails, instant messages, meeting transcripts and their ongoing chats with Faraday itself. The company then uses this data to build a better version of Faraday. Though Inherent pledges to keep humans involved in this elaborate process, many other companies are building similar technology, and some leading researchers believe A.I. systems will eventually be powerful enough to improve themselves with little or no help from human developers — a mind-bending goal that computer scientists call recursive self-improvement, or R.S.I. Two Silicon Valley start-ups — each valued at $4 billion — are proudly pursuing this dream, and leading labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are chasing it too.

entries.content: 4. Maintenance planning meets weather forecasting: Aligning repair schedules with climate forecasts. Some aspects of the traditional coal mining industry need to adapt to climatic conditions to maintain efficiency and output. Climate change can involve long-term shifts in temperatures and weather patterns. By using extended forecasting to address weather impact, mining organisations may predict when changes in temperature and sudden rains are likely to occur and take appropriate action. The mining industry is transitioning from traditional, calendar-based repair schedules to a more sophisticated, data-driven approach. \* Integrating data streams: Strategies combine short-term weather, long-term climate and equipment condition data. Short-term weather forecasting helps mining teams to determine operational limits. When telematics readings combine with IoT sensors, operational managers can use predictive maintenance to prevent breakdowns, reduce downtime and safeguard production schedules.

entries.title: In 1963, a plane flew to space. Why couldn’t we go farther?
entries.content:
In 1926, when [Albert Scott Crossfield](https://www.nasa.gov/people/a-scott-crossfield/) was five years old, a priest came to his home to administer the last rites. Suffering from an advanced case of pneumonia that had scarred his lungs and attacked his heart, the young Crossfield was drifting in and out of a coma when his parents summoned Father Skiperelli. They feared their son would not make it through the night.

Despite his delirium, Crossfield [distinctly remembered](https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/78431) Father “Skip” noting how the pictures of airplanes plastered across his bedroom walls were crowding out a symbol of the Sacred Heart. Crossfield survived but struggled with his health for years, which often confined him to bed rest. A doctor told him he would likely never pass a flight physical exam.

When he was nine years old, Crossfield outfitted a wicker chair in the family’s backyard with a cockpit-like control stick and rudder pedals, practicing for hours at a time. He would follow the instructions of a flight book propped on the chair’s arm, imagining himself soaring across oceans and over mountains, setting world records.

In 1953, Crossfield realized those childhood dreams when he steered a research plane, the [Douglas D-558-II Skyrocket](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-dryden-flight-research-center-news-room-news-releases-50th-anniversary-of-first-mach-2-flight-recalled/), to Mach 2, twice the speed of sound, making him the fastest person alive to date. Six years later, he was the first to pilot the X-15, a new experimental aircraft that was the world’s first plane to fly into [space](https://www.popsci.com/category/space/). But reaching space and staying there are different problems.

We’ve spent more than half a century since trying to take that next step—flying planes from a runway into orbit. After decades of disappointment, spaceplanes have found their place. On the edge.

## The edge of space—defined

In February 1963, an 81-year-old Hungarian émigré paused before making his way down the steps of the White House to receive the [first National Medal of Science from President Kennedy](https://www.jfklibrary.org/asset-viewer/archives/jfkwha-165-002). Kennedy reached to offer a hand. [Theodore von Kármán](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/who-we-are/faces-of-leadership-the-directors-of-jpl/dr-theodore-von-karman-1881-1963/) waved him off with [a witty remark](https://archive.org/details/windbeyondtheo00vonk/page/n13/mode/2up): “Mr. President, one does not need help going down, only going up.”

By then, von Kármán had become the 20th century’s preeminent aerodynamicist, an expert in going up. Von Kármán came to the U.S. in the 1920s to help expand the California Institute of [Technology](https://www.popsci.com/category/technology/)’s aviation research. At Caltech, he took charge of a band of student rocket experimenters known as the [Suicide Squad](https://magazine.caltech.edu/esblog/jplthe-suicide-squads-first-mission) for the hazards of their research. During World War II, their workshop became the [Jet Propulsion Laboratory](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/who-we-are/faces-of-leadership-the-directors-of-jpl/dr-theodore-von-karman-1881-1963/), eventually funded by [NASA](https://www.popsci.com/category/nasa/).

![NACA pilot A. Scott Crossfield next to the D-558-2 after first Mach 2 flight.](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/NACA_pilot_A._Scott_Crossfield_next_to_the_D-558-2_after_first_Mach_2_flight_E53-1113.jpg?strip=all&quality=85&amp%3Bw=2048)

Pilot A. Scott Crossfield stands next to the D-558-2 after first Mach 2 flight. *Image: [Public Domain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Scott_Crossfield#/media/File:NACA_pilot_A._Scott_Crossfield_next_to_the_D-558-2_after_first_Mach_2_flight_(E53-1113).jpg)* NASA

While von Kármán’s students were experimenting with rockets in California’s arroyos, a European contemporary, [Eugen Sänger](https://nmspacemuseum.org/inductee/eugen-sanger/), was testing rocket engines at the University of Technology in Vienna. During WWII, Sänger teamed up with German physicist [Irene Bredt](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0094576504001298) to design a spaceplane bomber for German High Command. Based on concepts from [*Raketenflugtechnik (Rocket Flight Engineering)*](https://www.historyofinformation.com/detail.php?id=2542), Sänger’s 1933 treatise and the first theoretical study of spaceplanes, the bomber would be capable of skipping across the edge of space like a stone on a lake. Their unfulfilled goal was to drop bombs on America.

After WWII ended, Sänger and Bredt’s work prompted the U.S. and other nations to explore skip-glide spaceplanes. Meanwhile, von Kármán sought to answer a very simple question: How high can an airplane fly before it stops being an airplane?

Because [Earth](https://www.popsci.com/10-ways-you-can-prove-earth-is-round/)’s atmosphere doesn’t have an abrupt end—it just thins until traces of it drift past the moon—von Kármán offered a practical demarcation point. A wing works by pushing air down; the thinner the atmosphere, the faster the wing must move to push enough of it. Climb high enough, von Kármán reasoned, and a wing would have to fly so fast to hold its own weight up that it would already be traveling at orbital speed—roughly 17,500 miles per hour at the bottom of low Earth orbit, or 100 miles above the surface. At that velocity, a wing becomes moot. The object isn’t being held aloft by air pressure at all; it’s continuously falling, tugged by Earth’s gravity, but moving sideways fast enough to keep missing Earth. Too slow and it spirals back down; too fast and it sails off into space.

Von Kármán calculated that crossover at around 50 miles up, though the number drifts with fluctuations in atmospheric density. In the 1960s, the Fédération Aéronautique Internationale rounded it to 100 kilometers, or 62 miles. NASA and the Air Force still use 50 miles. Regardless of the precise figure, it has become known as the edge of space, a turbulent shoreline where the physics of flying shift dramatically. Although no treaty has ever made it official, the [Kármán line](https://www.britannica.com/science/Karman-line) serves as the conventional divide between aviation law and space law, where wings serve no purpose in keeping an object aloft—only speed matters.

Getting to space requires altitude, but staying there requires speed. The gap between them is where the dream of the spaceplane has always faltered, beginning with the novel machine Crossfield helped design in the 1950s.

## The Incredible X-15

“Starting a flight in the X-15 is like starting your car while falling off a cliff,” wrote [*Popular Science*](https://books.google.com/books?id=TyQDAAAAMBAJ&lpg=PA212&pg=PA78#v=onepage&q&f=false) editor Wesley S. Griswold in 1963. The plane would take off from a runway, hanging from a pylon under the wing of a B-52 bomber until it reached an altitude of 45,000 feet. There, it would detach and its engine would ignite, hurling it upward “as though shot out of a cannon.”

![Black and white magazine image of plane.](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/x-15-space-plane.png?strip=all&quality=85)

The X-15 aerospace research plane falls away from the wind pylon of a B-52 mother plane over the Nevada desert. *Image: [Popular Science, June 1963 issue](https://books.google.ca/books?id=TyQDAAAAMBAJ&lpg=PA212&pg=PA78&redir_esc=y#v=twopage&q&f=false)*

A cross between a rocket and a plane, the [engineers](https://www.popsci.com/category/engineering/) building the X-15 called it a “missile with a cockpit,” Griswold reported in a [1958 preview for *Popular Science*](https://books.google.com/books?id=wiUDAAAAMBAJ&lpg=PP1&pg=PA110#v=onepage&q&f=false). Like a rocket, the plane was mostly a fuel tank. Like a plane, its stubby wings and tail fins enabled it to negotiate Earth’s atmosphere. The vessel’s most telling feature, however, was its twin sets of flight controls: one for navigating air, the other for space. As the plane approached the Kármán line, the pilot switched from traditional airplane controls to jets of superheated steam in the nose and wings, pointing the airplane with thrusters, just like a spacecraft.

When Scott Crossfield learned of the X-15 program around 1955, he left his government post at the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics, NASA’s predecessor, to work for North American Aviation, the X-15’s builder. There, Crossfield helped design the machine and became its first test pilot. He survived an engine explosion on the ground, which required the machine to undergo extensive repairs, and a landing that snapped the fuselage in two. By the time the plane was handed over to the joint U.S. Air Force-Navy-NASA program, he’d topped out at 88,116 feet, about 17 miles up. The plane had flown well short of space, but it was ready. Crossfield’s part was done.

Air Force pilot Bob White took the X-15 to space first, reaching 314,750 feet in July 1962, earning the first astronaut wings ever awarded to a winged aircraft pilot. NASA pilot Joe Walker flew the X-15 to 354,200 feet in August 1963—67 miles up, an altitude no winged aircraft has beaten, and one of only two X-15 flights to clear the Kármán line. Air Force pilot Pete Knight pushed the X-15 to Mach 6.7 in October 1967, still the fastest a piloted airplane has ever flown. In all, 13 flights crossed 50 miles—space’s threshold by NASA’s standards. Eight pilots earned astronaut wings, among them a NASA research pilot named Neil Armstrong.

Theodore von Kármán did not live to see Walker cross his eponymous line, the official edge of space. He died ten weeks earlier, in May 1963.

Amidst the X-15’s remarkable flights, in September 1965, Wernher von Braun, the director of NASA’s George C. Marshall Space Flight Center, penned [a feature for *Popular Science*](https://books.google.com/books?id=viUDAAAAMBAJ&lpg=PA69&pg=PA68#v=onepage&q&f=false) that predicted the coming era of spaceplanes. “Re-usable launch vehicles, looking more like airplanes than rockets, will boost manned and unmanned craft into orbit,” he wrote. But von Braun also hedged his prediction, claiming that such planes might not take off from a runway; they would be launched vertically on a booster.

## The spaceplane graveyard

In his 1986 State of the Union address, Ronald Reagan promised a “[new Orient Express](https://www.nytimes.com/2014/10/21/science/25-years-ago-nasa-envisioned-its-own-orient-express.html),” a spaceplane capable of reaching low Earth orbit. It would also take off from Washington, D.C., and reach Tokyo in two hours. The [Rockwell X-30](https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/rockwell-x-30/), the hypersonic aircraft designed to fulfill Reagan’s vision, would be powered by a scramjet engine, which captures oxygen from the air rather than carrying it in a tank. It was never built.

Britain pursued its own spaceplane program, dubbed [HOTOL](https://www.aerotime.aero/articles/hotol-british-space-plane-review-history) for Horizontal Take-Off and Landing. It never left the drawing board. West Germany designed [Sänger II](https://www.icas.org/icas_archive/ICAS1988/ICAS-88-1.5.1.pdf), named for the man whose 1930s skip-glide concept helped inspire spaceplane technology. It was cancelled before production.

A recent and promising winged attempt to reach orbit was [Reaction Engines](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c5y5zg85wnlo), a British company that took up where HOTOL left off and succeeded in getting the hardest part of a hypersonic engine working. But it failed to raise enough funding to build its spaceplane.

After Reagan’s X-30 program failed, NASA tried again, hiring [Lockheed Martin to build the X-33](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20110016255/downloads/20110016255.pdf), a test vehicle part of NASA’s [Venture Star](https://www.nasa.gov/gallery/x-33-venture-star-advanced-technology-demonstrator/) program. The X-ee would launch like a rocket, using its own engines, and fly like an airplane when descending. The program was canceled in 2001.

In 1999, *Popular Science* writer Bill Sweetman [profiled Space Access](https://books.google.com/books?id=gJfxBTKptj0C&lpg=PA75&pg=PA72#v=onepage&q&f=false), a Palmdale, California, startup founded by Rockwell engineer Steven Wurst, who had come out of the defunct X-30 program.

![Magazine two page spread showing an illustration of a space plane releasing a smaller space aircraft.](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/space-plane-space-access.png?strip=all&quality=85)

In 1999, Popular Science writer Bill Sweetman profiled Space Access, a Palmdale, California, startup founded by Rockwell engineer Steven Wurst, who had come out of the defunct X-30 program. *Image: [Popular Science, June 1999 issue](https://books.google.ca/books?id=gJfxBTKptj0C&lpg=PA75&pg=PA72&redir_esc=y#v=twopage&q&f=false)*

“It’s the flight rate, stupid,” Wurst told Sweetman. Unless a spacecraft flies often, it will never be cheap enough to be competitive. Wurst was right about the economics but wrong about the shape. An airplane light enough to fly well can’t carry enough propellant to reach orbit, and a vehicle carrying enough propellant to reach orbit is no longer much of an airplane. Two decades later, [Space X](https://www.popsci.com/category/spacex/) proved the point with [a reusable rocket that lands on its tail](https://www.popsci.com/spacex-reuse-rockets-now-what/).

## Shuttles—part plane, part payload

The term “spaceplane” has relaxed from its mid-20th century meaning to include shuttles—aircraft that are launched into space on the backs of rockets but have wings that enable them to return to runways.

From 1981 to 2011, the [U.S. Space Shuttle](https://www.nasa.gov/space-shuttle/) flew 135 missions to space, landed on runways, and looked like a plane. But it never took off like one. It went up vertically, riding on a disposable tank and recoverable rocket boosters, just as von Braun predicted, because the shuttle’s own engines could never have lifted it into space or achieved orbital velocity. As a payload fitted with wings and roughly 24,000 finicky thermal tiles that required manual inspection after every mission, it was too elaborate and expensive to continue operating.

But a new generation of shuttles has improved the economics. Smaller, uncrewed, and equipped with a more reliable heat shield, the [X-37B](https://www.boeing.com/space/x37b) looks like a mini Space Shuttle. It has completed seven missions since 2010. Its eighth was launched atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 in August 2025. Using a similar design, Sierra Space’s [Dream Chaser](https://www.sierraspace.com/dream-chaser-spaceplane/uncrewed-cargo-spacecraft/) shuttle is scheduled to debut in late 2026.

## Spaceplanes find their place

Despite decades of failed programs, true spaceplanes have begun to carve out an important niche, traveling at hypersonic speeds to extreme altitudes and the edge of space but not into orbit.

[Dawn Aerospace’s Aurora](https://www.dawnaerospace.com/spaceplane) is a tiny rocket-powered suborbital spaceplane that takes off from and lands on conventional runways, which is the whole point. Operating under remote control—it’s too small for a crew—it has flown 64 times since 2016, occasionally twice in one day. In November 2024, it became the first civilian aircraft to fly supersonic since Concorde. It has carried research payloads for Johns Hopkins, Arizona State, and the Royal New Zealand Navy. Future versions are designed to exceed Mach 3.5 and cross the Kármán line—twice a day.

Just like the X-15 nearly 70 years ago, California-based [Stratolaunch](https://www.stratolaunch.com/mission/) drops its Talon-A hypersonic research spaceplane from beneath the wing of the world’s largest airplane. Similarly, [Virgin Galactic](https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2026/05/06/virgin-galactic-spaceplane-photo-space-tourism/89927374007/)’s suborbital aircraft is dropped from a plane, firing its own rocket engine to transport sightseeing customers to the edge of space, before landing on a runway in New Mexico.

![A weird looking plane with four tails flies over the desert.](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Virgin-Galactic-space-plane.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

Virgin Galactic’s WhiteKnightTwo and SpaceShipTwo in flight during captive carry test flight at Mojave on July 15, 2010 in California. *Image: Virgin Galactic / Contributor / Getty Images* Virgin Galactic

## A rich shoreline

The edge of space offers more than just sightseeing. Since it requires traveling at multiple Mach speeds to remain aloft, spaceplanes are on the cutting edge of hypersonic research, experiencing conditions that can’t be replicated in terrestrial wind tunnels. The edge of space also offers microgravity conditions, which are vital for research.

The thermosphere, where the Kármán line falls, is among the least studied layers of our atmosphere—too high for research aircraft, too low for satellites—yet it matters for climate models and for the safety of spacecraft passing through. And, while an “Orient Express” from Washington, D.C., to Tokyo in two hours remains a dream, plumbing the shoreline of space may teach us enough about hypersonics and Earth’s upper atmosphere to someday make it real.

## X-15 redux—from runway to the edge of space and back

On April 19, 2006, Scott Crossfield took off from Prattville, Alabama, flying his own Cessna 210A, heading home to Virginia. He was 84 years old and still flying himself to speaking engagements, evangelizing for aerospace education. He was [killed over northern Georgia](https://www.aopa.org/news-and-media/all-news/2007/september/27/ntsb-releases-final-report-on-crossfield-crash) when his airplane came apart in a line of thunderstorms.

Having nearly succumbed to pneumonia as a boy, Crossfield had survived a rocket engine detonating behind him on a test stand and walked away from a landing that broke his airplane in half. He had flown the most dangerous aircraft ever built, flying faster than any human at the time. What finally killed him was Earth’s own atmosphere, the place of his childhood dreams, and the medium wings were made for.

For more than half a century after Crossfield’s X-15 debut, engineers have kept trying to build planes that could bridge the physics of atmosphere and space, not only taking off and landing on conventional runways but also orbiting Earth. Yet our propulsion technology does not support coupling atmospheric lift with extreme orbital speed. If it did, we’d likely be flying in saucers, not planes. In the end, the X-15 had the spaceplane’s destination right all along: surfing the atmospheric shoreline along the edge of space.

*In* [*A Century in Motion*](https://www.popsci.com/century-in-motion/)*, Popular Science revisits fascinating transportation stories from our archives, from hybrid cars to moving sidewalks, and explores how these inventions are re-emerging today in surprising ways.*

entries.title: iPhone Duo a godsend for mini iPhone fans, minus the price
entries.content:
After years of fans complaining that the beloved iPhone mini disappeared, Apple brought back a pint-sized phone that costs as much as a MacBook Pro. I want one.  
  

![Apple product showcase collage featuring the iPhone Duo, iOS interface previews, camera features, titanium design, battery life, display sizes, vapor chamber cooling, and lifestyle photos in rounded rectangles](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/68995-145506-Apple-Event——September-9-1-16-57-screenshot-xl.jpg)  
All of these cool features and I'll just need to pony up four months of my mortgage

  
You may remember me as the author of [nearly 3,000](https://appleinsider.com/articles/25/02/20/apple-could-have-sold-me-an-iphone-se-4-but-it-wont-sell-me-the-iphone-16e) words about how the [iPhone 16e](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone-16e "iPhone 16e") seemed like a stupid product. You also may remember that a large portion of that rant was, more or less, me yelling about how Apple should have never discontinued a small iPhone SE or the iPhone mini.  
  
After I wrote my iPhone 16e piece, the one thing that surprised me was the number of people who *also* missed the iPhone mini. There were a lot of you.  
  
  
 [Continue Reading on AppleInsider](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/09/17/iphone-duo-a-godsend-for-mini-iphone-fans-minus-the-price?utm_source=rss) | [Discuss on our Forums](https://forums.appleinsider.com/discussion/245713?urm_source=rss)

entries.title: Give developers time to update apps for iPhone Duo
entries.content:
Apple makes it sound easy to update apps for the new [iPhone Duo](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone-duo "iPhone Duo"). It's going to take some developers longer, not everything will work well at first, and some won't do it at all.  
  

![Person holding a smartphone horizontally, viewing a screen with educational flashcard-style apps, while sitting at a wooden table with a smoothie and a bowl of fruit in the background](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/69024-145531-000-lede-bad-apps-xl.jpg)  
This is what you paid $2,000 for? Give it time: developers can have a lot to do to make their apps take proper advantage of the iPhone Duo - image elements credit: Apple.

  
Even though everyone believed a foldable [iPhone](https://appleinsider.com/inside/iphone "iPhone") was coming, Apple did manage to keep the iPhone Duo secret [better than usual](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/09/11/ternus-and-joswiak-talk-about-designing-the-iphone-duo-in-secret). Which means that as well as surprising buyers, it can have startled most developers.  
  
Not all, of course, as Apple reached out to ones such as Netflix in order to have third-party apps to show at the launch. Then, too, when Apple insists that updating apps to work on the new device is straightforward, it means if developers have already been following its guidelines.  
  
  
 [Continue Reading on AppleInsider](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/09/17/give-developers-time-to-update-apps-for-iphone-duo?utm_source=rss) | [Discuss on our Forums](https://forums.appleinsider.com/discussion/245712?urm_source=rss)

entries.title: AI can reach Addigy's iPhone management layer, assuming you let it
entries.content:
AI-assisted scripting, reporting, compliance controls, and MCP support are coming to Addigy's Apple device-management platform, with administrators still required to approve management actions before they run.  
  

![Open silver MacBook with Apple logo on a desk, next to a black VR headset and small black box, against a softly lit blue and purple background](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/68999-145448-M5-MacBook-Pro-back-xl.jpg)M5 MacBook Pro

  
Addigy Intelligence Suite launches September 17 with AI Script Assist, natural-language reporting, controls for unapproved AI applications, and support for Model Context Protocol. Administrators must approve proposed management actions before they run.  
  
The approval requirement keeps the system from acting autonomously. Administrators remain responsible for reviewing AI-generated scripts or proposed actions before changes reach managed devices.  
  
AI Script Assist can generate scripts, review existing code, and recommend management actions. Administrators can describe a task in plain language instead of writing every command manually.  
  
  
 [Continue Reading on AppleInsider](https://appleinsider.com/articles/26/09/17/ai-can-now-reach-addigys-device-management-layer-with-approval-required?utm_source=rss) | [Discuss on our Forums](https://forums.appleinsider.com/discussion/245711?urm_source=rss)

entries.title: How to downgrade iOS 27 to iOS 26 on your iPhone
entries.content:
[Macworld](https://www.macworld.com)

Apple updates iOS every year, bestowing upon our iPhones a range of new features and security improvements, as well as the occasional redesign. In September 2026, [iOS 27](https://www.macworld.com/article/2986799/ios-27-features-compatiblity-siri-ai-updates.html) made its debut. Most iPhone users will move to the new platform straight away, and the majority are likely to love the changes. But what if you encounter bugs, poor battery life, or another problem that makes you wish you could return to iOS 26?

And what if subsequent iOS 27 updates may also introduce problems that leave you wishing you could return to an earlier version?

Downgrading from iOS 27 may be possible, but only while Apple continues to sign a compatible version of iOS 26—or an earlier release of iOS 27—for your particular iPhone. There is usually only a short window in which this can be done.

In this article, we explore your options for downgrading iOS on an iPhone. Be aware that the process has significant disadvantages: it erases the device, and a backup made after installing iOS 27 generally cannot be restored to an iPhone running iOS 26.

With just one click, it lists out all the available firmware versions that Apple is still signing, so that you’re able to decide which version is your favorite or downgrade to any ideal version. The downgrade is completed without iTunes. Now 25% OFF by using code: MACWORLD25.

[Free Trial](https://down.easeus.com/product/mobixpert_system_repair?ref=https%3A%2F%2Fmobi.easeus.com%2Fmobitoolkit%2Fios-system-repair.html%3Fcjevent%3Didg-foundry&gclid=idg-foundry&gclid_type=cjevent)

[Buy and Save 25%](http://www.jdoqocy.com/click-8752386-15626909?sid=rss)

## Can you downgrade iOS 27?

The answer depends on whether you want to return from iOS 27 to iOS 26, remove an iOS beta, or reverse a recent point update. A downgrade may be possible in each of these situations, but usually only for a limited time.

The main factor is whether Apple is still signing the older version for your exact iPhone model. Signing is Apple’s way of authorizing a particular iOS release for installation on a particular device. Once Apple stops signing a release, you cannot install it using the standard restore process, even if you have already downloaded the correct firmware file.

Apple typically stops signing an older version of iOS soon after releasing its replacement. If you act quickly enough, however, you may be able to return to the previous version. We explain how below.

For example, shortly after installing iOS 27, it may be possible to return to iOS 26.7, which Apple released alongside iOS 27 on September 14, 2026. This will work only while Apple continues to sign iOS 26.7 for your iPhone model.

### Reasons you may not be able to downgrade

* **Apple is no longer signing the older version**: Once Apple stops signing a release, you cannot install it using the standard restore process. This means you cannot return to much earlier releases such as iOS 26 or iOS 18 after their signing windows have closed.
* **Your iPhone came with iOS 27 installed**: An iPhone cannot be downgraded to a version of iOS that was never released for that model. New iPhones that shipped with iOS 27—including the iPhone 18 generation—cannot ordinarily be downgraded to iOS 26, even if Apple continues to sign iOS 26 for older models.
* **The firmware is not intended for your iPhone**: You can install only an IPSW firmware file created for your exact iPhone model and still signed by Apple.

## What you need to know before downgrading iOS 27

Before you try to roll back your iPhone from iOS 27 to iOS 26, be aware of the following limitations:

1. **The downgrade will erase your iPhone:** Reverting to an older version of iOS requires wiping the apps and data from the device.
2. **A backup made after installing iOS 27 cannot be restored to iOS 26:** Backups contain settings, app data, databases, and other information formatted for the version of iOS on which they were created. If you don’t have a compatible older backup, you will need to set up the iPhone as new. Information synchronized separately through iCloud should become available again after you sign in.
3. **New iPhone models cannot run iOS 26:** If your iPhone model first shipped with iOS 27, it cannot be downgraded to iOS 26.
4. **Apple’s signing window can close at any time:** You need to act quickly. Downloading the required IPSW file while Apple is still signing it does not guarantee that you can install it later. If Apple has stopped signing the release by the time you attempt the restore, the process will fail.
5. **You may remove important security improvements:** Downgrading can leave your iPhone without security fixes included in the newer release. It may be safer to wait for the next iOS 27 update to see whether it resolves the problem that made you consider downgrading.

## How to downgrade iOS: What you need

Before beginning the downgrade process, make sure you have the necessary equipment, software, and backups ready.

### 1) Find out whether Apple is still signing the older version of iOS

The first thing you need to do is find out if Apple is still signing the version of iOS you need.

To find out whether Apple is still signing the version of iOS you need, [visit this page](https://ipsw.me/product/iPhone) and look up your exact iPhone model to see which versions are still signed by Apple. Apple usually stops signing a version of iOS within one or two weeks of a new update. Signing status and available firmware can differ between devices.

![iOS still being signed](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/iPhone-17-ios-still-being-signed.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Find the version of iOS you want.

Foundry

If you are lucky and the old version is still being signed, you will be able to downgrade.

However, you still may prefer to stay on the new version because this process will wipe your iPhone.

### 2) Download the correct IPSW firmware files

You will need the correct firmware for your iPhone model.

To do this go to [IPSW.me](https://ipsw.me/product/iPhone) (on your Mac) and download the correct version of the iOS you want that matches your iPhone model.

As said above, it needs to still be signed by Apple at the time you wish to restore that version, which can be a very narrow window indeed – days, not weeks.

The software should start downloading to your Downloads folder. Note, it can take a long time to download an iOS firmware file and the IPSW file may be around 10GB or more, so make sure the computer has enough free storage.

Downloading a signed IPSW now will not preserve your ability to use it after Apple closes the signing window

### 3) A Mac or PC

You will need to use the Finder on a Mac or the Apple Devices App on a PC to restore your iPhone.

You should also ensure that macOS is up-to-date on your Mac, or that the latest version of Apple Devices is installed on your Windows PC.

An appropriate [USB-C or Lightning cable](https://www.macworld.com/article/2051607/usb-c-charging-cables-iphone-ipad-mac.html) will also be necessary to connect the iPhone to the computer.

### 4) A backup from before the update

The only way to install an older version of iOS is to erase the version currently installed on your iPhone. If you want to recover your apps, settings, and other data afterward, you will need a compatible backup.

The main problem is that a backup created under iOS 27 generally cannot be restored to an iPhone running iOS 26. To recover everything after downgrading, you need a backup created before you installed iOS 27. This is why we recommend backing up your iPhone to a Mac and archiving that backup before updating iOS.

If your iPhone has not been backed up since you installed iOS 27, an older compatible backup may still be available. Here’s how to check:

### How to find an iCloud backup on your iPhone:

1. Open Settings.
2. Tap your name.
3. Tap iCloud.
4. Scroll down and tap iCloud Backup.
5. Swipe down to All Device Backups and tap your iPhone.
6. Check the date of the latest backup to determine whether it was made before you installed iOS 27.

iCloud does not provide a collection of archived backups for each device in the same way that a Mac can. If iCloud has backed up your iPhone since you installed iOS 27, the older iOS 26 backup may already have been replaced.

For more guidance, see [How to restore an iPhone from a backup](https://www.macworld.com/article/672439/how-to-restore-an-iphone-or-ipad-from-an-icloud-or-itunes-backup.html).

### How to find an archived backup on a Mac:

If you archived an older backup on your Mac, here’s how to find it:

1. Connect the iPhone to the Mac with a USB cable.
2. Open Finder.
3. Select the iPhone in the sidebar.
4. Click General.
5. Click Manage Backups.
6. Locate the archived backup, checking its date to make sure it was created before you installed iOS 27.

After downgrading you can restore this archived back up via the Finder, we’ll explain how to do that below.

If you don’t have an older backup, it is still worth making a fresh iOS 27 backup before beginning the downgrade. You won’t be able to restore that backup while the iPhone is running iOS 26, but it will allow you to recover your current data if you later reinstall iOS 27.

You can still downgrade (as long as iOS 26 remains signed) without a compatible older backup, but you will need to set up the iPhone as new. Information synchronized separately through iCloud—such as contacts, calendars, files in iCloud Drive, and iCloud Photos—should become available again after you sign in. However, you should not assume that every app or item of data will return.

### 5) Your Apple Account details

Make sure you have the password for the Aple Account associated with the iPhone or you may encounter issues with Activation Lock and be unable to complete the setup process once your iPhone restarts.

## How to downgrade iOS 27: Step-by-step guide

![How to downgrade iOS on iPhone](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/Downgrade-iOS-on-iPhone.jpg?quality=50&strip=all)

This is what it looked like when we downgraded from iOS 16.6.1 to iOS 16.6. The process is the same – as long as the old version is still signed.

Foundry

The steps below explain how to downgrade from iOS 27 to a signed version of iOS 26, such as iOS 26.7. The process is the same when moving from a newer point release to an immediately preceding release, provided Apple is still signing the version you want.

**WARNING: This process will wipe your iPhone! Beware that you could lose your data if you don’t have a backup from before the iOS update you are downgrading from**.

1. Make a fresh backup of the iPhone before proceeding. Remember that an iOS 27 backup cannot normally be restored to iOS 26, but it will preserve your current data if you later install iOS 27.
2. Download the version of iOS you require from [IPSW.me](http://IPSW.me).
3. On a Mac, open the Finder. On a PC, use the Apple Devices app.
4. Plug in your iPhone using a suitable cable. If asked, unlock the iPhone and confirm that you trust the computer.
5. Turn off Find My on your device because it enables Activation Lock, which could prevent you from erasing and downgrading the iPhone. Go to Settings > your name > Find My > Find My iPhone > Turn Off. Enter your Apple Account password to confirm.
6. Select the iPhone in the Finder sidebar or Apple Devices app.
7. Hold down the Option/Alt key and click Restore iPhone. On a PC, hold Shift and click Restore iPhone.
8. Select the version of iOS you wish to install on the iPhone from your Downloads folder.
9. Click Open.
10. A message will appear saying which version of iOS you will install – this should be the one you selected. Click to confirm and wait while your iPhone is restored. Do not disconnect the iPhone during this process.
11. The phone will be wiped and the older version of iOS installed on the iPhone.
12. You now need to set up your iPhone again. Be aware that backups made on newer versions of iOS usually can’t be restored to older versions, so you may need to set up the iPhone as new.
13. If you have a compatible backup made while the iPhone was running iOS 26, choose the option to restore from that backup during setup. Otherwise, select the option to set up the iPhone without transferring apps and data, then sign in to your Apple Account.

If the restore reports that the iPhone is not eligible for the requested build, check that you downloaded the IPSW for the correct model. If the file is correct, it is probably the case that Apple has stopped signing that version and the downgrade is no longer possible.

## What to do if the iOS downgrade fails

![Apple iPhone 17e review 16](https://b2c-contenthub.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Apple-iPhone-17e-review-16.jpg?quality=50&strip=all&w=1200)

Don’t toss your iPhone away because it won’t downgrade.

Britta O’Boyle

If you were unable to downgrade your iPhone it could have been for one of the following reasons:

### The iPhone isn’t eligible for the requested build

Apple is either no longer signing the selected release, or you downloaded the IPSW for the wrong iPhone model.

Return to IPSW.me, select your exact model and confirm that the release is shown as signed.

### Apple has stopped signing the version

In this case there is no supported way to complete the downgrade.

### The backup requires a newer version of iOS

If your backup was created using iOS 27 you won’t be able to restore it to iOS 26. You either need an older compatible backup or you need other set up the iPhone as new, or you could upgrade your iPhone to iOS 27 again and restoring the newer backup.

### The Mac or PC doesn’t recognize the iPhone

You need to unlock the iPhone and tap Trust if prompted.

If that doesn’t solve the problem, try another cable or USB port – avoiding an unpowered hub.

If it’s still not recognised, check macOS is up-to-date and restart both devices.

If the iPhone still does not appear, place it into recovery mode using the instructions here: [How to put an iPhone in Recovery mode](https://www.macworld.com/article/672701/how-to-put-an-iphone-into-recovery-mode.html).

### The restore is stuck or the iPhone shows the Apple logo

Leave the iPhone connected and give the restore a little more time to finish.

If it does not progress, restart the computer, reconnect the iPhone and try using recovery mode (as per the link above).

Do not disconnect the iPhone while Finder or Apple Devices indicates that the restore is still taking place.

## FAQ

---

1.

### Why can’t I downgrade to an older version of iOS?

There is a very small window in which you can downgrade.

When software is made available by Apple, the company includes a signature that confirms its authenticity. This is for security reasons, so that you won’t accidentally install bogus software that claims to be iOS and then find yourself in a world of pain as all your data is stolen.

Whereas in the past Apple would leave the signature valid on previous versions of iOS for a short time, in recent years the signature has been removed within days of, and sometimes almost simultaneously with, the release of the newer version.

If the version of iOS you wish to reinstall doesn’t have this signature, then you will not be able to install it on your iPhone or iPad.

2.

### Is there another way to go back to a previous version of iOS if this doesn’t work?

If you simply *must* have a certain version of iOS, perhaps because an old app is stuck on that version and hasn’t been updated since, then there is a somewhat drastic solution. [Buy an old iPhone.](https://www.macworld.com/article/670952/how-to-buy-second-hand-refurbished-iphone.html)

It sounds silly, but it’s probably the easiest way to ensure that you have the iOS version you need. We’d recommend scouring [eBay](https://www.ebay.com/?mkcid=1&mkrid=711-53200-19255-0&siteid=0&campid=5339153163&customid=rss&toolid=10001&mkevt=1) or some of the refurbished outlets like [Amazon Renewed](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=renewed+cellular+phone&rh=n%3A2335752011%2Cp_89%3AApple&dc4&tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com) (or [Back Market](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=25205&awinaffid=254429&clickref=rss&ued=https://www.backmarket.co.uk/en-gb), [MusicMagpie](https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=5792&awinaffid=254429&clickref=rss&ued=https://www.musicmagpie.co.uk/store/apple-iphone-store), or [Amazon Renewed](https://www.amazon.co.uk/s?i=specialty-aps&srs=8362590031&rh=p_89%3AApple&pf_rd_i=8362590031&tag=macworld05-20&asc_refurl=https://www.macworld.com) in the U.K.) to see if someone is selling an older model still running the iOS you want. Needless to say, you should specifically ask the buyer to confirm this–don’t just assume that the iPhone will still be running the version of iOS that was current when it launched.

But bear in mind, finally, that there’s a reason why Apple wants people using its latest software. Not only does this mean you get the newest features and design, but it should also be the safest one available as it has the latest updates.

There are also third-party tools that can offer easier workflows, additional automation, or support for unsigned firmware. Examples include [EaseUS iOS System Repair](https://www.jdoqocy.com/click-100470607-15398169?sid=rss&url=https://mobi.easeus.com/mobitoolkit/ios-system-repair.html), [AnyFix](https://www.imobie.com/anyfix/ios-system-recovery.htm), [Tenorshare ReiBoot](https://www.tenorshare.com/products/reiboot.html), and [TinyUmbrella](https://tiny-umbrella.com).

3.

### How long does Apple allow you to downgrade iOS after an update?

Apple typically provides a very narrow window for downgrading your iPhone’s operating system.

This limitation exists because Apple is required to “sign” an older version of iOS to confirm its authenticity and security before it can be installed on a device.

Once Apple stops signing an older version, which often happens within days of a newer release, that version becomes unavailable for installation.

Apple’s official stance, as explained by senior vice president of software engineering Craig Federighi, is that downgrading is restricted because “each iOS update improves the security of your iPhone… To downgrade iOS means that your device would be less secure, and easier for hackers to get into.”

4.

### Can you downgrade iOS without a computer?

Downgrading an iPhone or iPad to an older version of iOS typically requires a computer, as Apple does not provide a native “rollback” feature within the device’s settings. While you can perform certain actions like removing a beta profile directly on your device, a true downgrade to a previous stable version generally necessitates a PC or Mac to install the necessary firmware files.

You can turn off Beta Updates directly on the iPhone, but doing so does not remove the beta already installed. To leave the beta immediately, you need to connect the iPhone to a computer, erase it and restore the current public release. See [How to remove the iOS Beta](https://www.macworld.com/article/1067004/how-to-remove-ios-beta-iphone.html).

5.

### Will downgrading iOS erase my iPhone?

Yes, downgrading iOS will typically erase your iPhone. The standard process for moving to an older version of the operating system requires a complete wipe of the device’s current data to ensure the older software can be installed cleanly.

Because of this, having a backup is critical. However, there is a significant limitation regarding compatibility: backups made on a newer version of iOS (such as iOS 26) cannot be restored to a device running an older version (such as iOS 18) . To get your data back after a downgrade, you must use a backup that was created while the device was still running that older version or earlier.

Make a new backup before beginning, even if it requires iOS 27. Although that backup will not restore to iOS 26, it will allow you to recover your current data if you subsequently reinstall iOS 27.

While official methods via Apple’s Finder involve wiping the device, some third-party software claims to offer “no data loss” downgrades. For instance, the program [Tenorshare ReiBoot](https://www.tenorshare.com/products/reiboot.html) is described as a tool that allows you to downgrade iOS 26 to 18 without data loss on your iPhone or iPad.

6.

### Can I restore an iOS 27 backup to iOS 26?

Apple does not support restoring a backup created using a newer version of iOS to a device running an older version. You will need a compatible backup made before you installed iOS 27, or you will have to set up the iPhone as new.

7.

### Can third-party software install an unsigned version of iOS?

Consumer restore utilities cannot ordinarily bypass Apple’s firmware-signing requirements on a modern iPhone. Some third-party tools can simplify parts of the restore process, but they still depend on Apple authorizing the firmware for your device.

Make an independent backup before using any third-party recovery utility.

entries.title: Fed Rate Bets Become a Robinhood Prediction-Market Favorite
entries.content:
![Abstract prediction-market display with red rate-decision marker before a central-bank building](https://readwrite.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/fed-rate-bets-robinhood-prediction-market-favorite-300x167.webp)

## Lead

Robinhood’s futures and prediction-markets vice president and general manager, JB Mackenzie, said trading activity in prediction markets was rising ahead of the Federal Reserve’s rate decision. In comments reported by [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/robinhood-predictions-vp-on-growth-in-event-contracts-ce785bd2da8bf422), citing MT Newswires, Mackenzie said interest in contracts tied to the Fed had grown substantially over the previous year.

The comments came as markets were pricing in roughly an 85% chance of a 25-basis-point hike, according to the report. Mackenzie discussed the activity with Romaine Bostick on Bloomberg’s The Close. He characterized Fed-related contracts as moving from relatively muted early adoption to one of Robinhood’s most popular contract categories.

The interview did not disclose specific trading-volume or revenue figures for contracts tied to the Fed. As a result, the reported popularity of those contracts should be read as Mackenzie’s description of activity within Robinhood’s broader event-contract offering rather than as a separate, quantified financial result.

## Deal or Result Detail

Separate reporting has described substantial growth in Robinhood’s overall event-contract business. Crypto Briefing reported that the business grew roughly 15 times year over year in August. The same report said Robinhood generated $156 million in event-contract revenue during the second quarter of 2026 and that 13.6 billion event contracts traded during that quarter.

Those figures cover the event-contract segment as a whole, not Fed-related contracts specifically. They therefore provide context for the scale of Robinhood’s broader activity but do not establish what portion of revenue or trading volume came from macroeconomic contracts.

## A widening product catalog

Robinhood’s event-contract offering has expanded from politically themed contracts into player-specific sports contracts and broader sporting-event outcomes, according to the supplementary reporting. That report also described an upcoming election hub, illustrating the range of categories associated with the company’s event-contract business.

In June 2026, Robinhood launched Rothera, described as a CFTC-licensed joint-venture exchange built for event contracts. The company also maintains partnerships with Kalshi and ForecastEx to route contracts, according to the same reporting. Together, those arrangements provide context for the infrastructure supporting Robinhood’s catalog.

## Competitive pressure builds

The available reporting centers on Robinhood’s own event-contract expansion and does not provide comparable, verified figures for other companies. For Robinhood, Mackenzie’s comments put Fed-related contracts within a broader business that has reported rapid growth, while leaving the specific contribution of any individual rate-decision market undisclosed.

That distinction is important as attention turns to the Federal Reserve decision. The reported activity indicates growing interest in Fed-linked contracts on Robinhood, but the available evidence does not show whether that interest will persist after the decision or how it compares with trading in the company’s other event categories.

The post [Fed Rate Bets Become a Robinhood Prediction-Market Favorite](https://readwrite.com/robinhood-prediction-markets/) appeared first on [ReadWrite](https://readwrite.com).

entries.title: SilkParasite Infrastructure Links SpiceRAT to Central Asian Targets
entries.content:
## Hunt.io links SpiceRAT, NodeEdgeRAT and NomadRAT to a four-year SilkParasite campaign targeting governments and critical sectors in Central Asia.

Hunt.io and researcher [Guy Yasur](https://x.com/Shto_ota) have traced a tight cluster of SpiceRAT command‑and‑control servers that predate and extend Bitdefender’s August 2026 SilkParasite report. The work doesn’t dissect malware samples; it maps the network side of the operation with enough precision to tie three of SilkParasite’s seven RAT families (SpiceRAT, NodeEdgeRAT, and NomadRAT) through shared certificates, domains, and hosting patterns.

*“Shared parent domains and an identical TLS certificate connect this infrastructure to hosts Bitdefender attributed to SpiceRAT, NodeEdgeRAT, and NomadRAT, three of the seven malware families documented in the SilkParasite report.” reads the [report](https://hunt.io/blog/silkparasite-spicerat-central-asia-infrastructure) published by Hunt.io.*

*“The certificate imitating the Uzbekistan railway entity was issued by TLC, a certificate authority wholly funded by CAICT, a Chinese state research institute under the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology.”*

In March 2026, Hunt.io identified five SpiceRAT command-and-control servers hosted by different providers and in different countries. Researchers linked them through several common elements, including the same hostnames, TLS certificates, and a cloned webpage used as the default page.

Instead of focusing only on the malware itself, this approach looks at the infrastructure behind it. Shared certificates or identical webpage hashes can provide strong and practical indicators that defenders can use to identify other servers linked to the campaign.

One certificate in particular stands out. It impersonates Uzbekistan’s state railway authority (azure.uzrailwaystax[.]com) and was issued by TLC DV TLS CA, a CA wholly funded by CAICT, a Chinese state research institute under the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. The issuer alone isn’t an indicator—nearly 3,000 servers host TLC certificates—but a domain‑validated cert spoofing a Central Asian state entity from a China‑based CA does suggest a deliberate procurement channel.

Requests to ns2.asiainfo.it[.]com on 188.190.29[.]126 returned a full copy of RTX Corporation’s homepage, complete with navigation, subsidiary links, and a stock ticker. The page contained no malicious code and wasn’t unique to that server, but its reuse across the cluster made it a powerful fingerprint.

*“Hunt.io’s C2 Infrastructure module tracks servers matching detection signatures for known malware families, including SpiceRAT. In mid-March 2026, we observed a cluster of five active SpiceRAT servers: [46.30.191[.]230](https://portal.hunt.io/ip/46.30.191.230), [188.190.29[.]126](https://portal.hunt.io/ip/188.190.29.126), [193.29.59[.]159](https://portal.hunt.io/ip/193.29.59.159), [31.58.220[.]250](https://portal.hunt.io/ip/31.58.220.250), and [171.22.16[.]187](https://portal.hunt.io/ip/171.22.16.187). The five were active together in mid-March 2026, across multiple hosting providers and countries.” continues the report.*

[![](https://i0.wp.com/securityaffairs.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-46.png?resize=1024%2C456&ssl=1)](https://i0.wp.com/securityaffairs.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/image-46.png?ssl=1)

A HuntSQL query on the page’s SHA‑256 hash returned exactly 13 hosts; three were already in Bitdefender’s SpiceRAT list, two more matched Hunt.io’s SpiceRAT signature, and the remaining eight extended the footprint through shared nginx versions and the same static page.

Why RTX? The report offers two plausible explanations: the page rendered cleanly and was grabbed as a convenient template, or it reflects shared tooling where the clone functions as a default deployment asset. Either way, for defenders it’s a low‑noise, high‑precision signature: byte‑for‑byte identical wherever it lands.

Bitdefender’s [SilkParasite](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/silkparasite) [**report**](https://www.bitdefender.com/en-gb/blog/businessinsights/silkparasite-tracking-china-nexus-apt-across-central-asia) treated several RAT families as distinct, but Hunt.io’s network view shows they share parent domains and certificates. For example, help.hoster‑kg[.]com (on 193.29.58[.]192) presented the same railway‑spoofing certificate, while Bitdefender attributed evo.hoster‑kg[.]com to NodeEdgeRAT; the two are linked through shared registration of hoster‑kg[.]com, not a shared server. Similarly, kg.tdtu[.]org shares a parent domain with mineconom.tdtu[.]org, a NomadRAT C2 indicator in the SilkParasite report.

This doesn’t prove a single operator, but it does show a support function or toolset shared across the campaign. From a detection standpoint, it means pivoting on domains, certificates, and hosting profiles can surface nodes that sample‑based analysis would miss.

The cluster’s domains don’t just look governmental; they spoof specific ministries and state enterprises. Examples include help.galkynysh[.]net (Galkynysh gas field, Turkmenistan), tmgaz‑server[.]com (Türkmengaz), tm‑mfa[.]com (Turkmenistan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs), and tojiktelecomtj[.]com (Tojiktelecom, Tajikistan). Additional domains impersonate Turkmen energy (sanly.oilgas‑tm[.]com), Uzbek administration (azure.adm‑devon[.]com), and even the Kyrgyz president’s residence (data.yntymak‑ordo[.]com).

Bitdefender’s targeting came from lures and infection telemetry; Hunt.io’s infrastructure analysis names the same sectors with concrete entities. Passive DNS and subdomain enumeration push the timeline back to mid‑2022, suggesting this isn’t a new campaign with a fresh brand—it’s a longer‑running operation now labeled SilkParasite.

SilkParasite overlaps with [FamousSparrow](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/famoussparrow), a suspected China‑nexus actor previously seen targeting hotels, governments, and international organizations. The infrastructure also mirrors IndigoZebra (Speccom), documented by Check Point in 2021 as targeting Central Asian ministries with similar domain patterns (mail, service, help) and overlapping naming conventions. These parallels don’t settle attribution, but they do reinforce a consistent operational style across China‑nexus activity in Central Asia.

If you’re responsible for OT/ICS, telecom, or government networks in the region, start by checking your edge and DMZ for the indicators below, especially the RTX page hash and the railway‑spoofing certificate. Monitor for high‑numbered RDP‑over‑TLS ports (64350, 64330, 65535, 65111) on the ASNs most prevalent in the cluster, and watch for domains impersonating local hosting providers or state entities. The original Hunt.io post includes the full IoC tables and HuntSQL queries; linking to it is essential for precise awareness and for teams that want to reproduce the pivots.

*“The targeting picture that emerges from this infrastructure, named ministries and state enterprises across five Central Asian countries dating back to at least mid-2022 suggests SilkParasite is a more recent label for an operation with much longer and wider footprint.” concludes the report. “Organizations in the affected sectors and regions can make use of the above indicators and observations to assess their own exposure.”*

**Follow me on Twitter:**[**@securityaffairs**](https://twitter.com/securityaffairs)**and**[**Facebook**](https://www.facebook.com/sec.affairs)**and**[**Mastodon**](https://infosec.exchange/@securityaffairs)

[**Pierluigi Paganini**](http://www.linkedin.com/pub/pierluigi-paganini/b/742/559)

**(**[**SecurityAffairs**](http://securityaffairs.co/wordpress/)**– hacking, SilkParasite)**
